    27	// OversizedCheckpointMetadataThreshold is the blob size above which a
    28	// per-session metadata.json on entire/checkpoints/v1 is reported by
    29	// `entire doctor`. GitHub warns at 50 MiB and refuses any blob over 100 MiB, and
    30	// a refused blob anywhere in the branch's history makes the whole branch
    31	// unpushable there — including through a forge's push mirror. A healthy
    32	// metadata.json is tens of kilobytes, so anything past this line is the
    33	// pre-v0.10.1 prompt_attributions bloat (see checkpoint.MaxPromptAttributionsBytes),
    34	// not a large session.
    35	const OversizedCheckpointMetadataThreshold int64 = 50 << 20
    36	
    37	// promptAttributionsField is the metadata.json key the shrink removes. It is
    38	// the only field whose size scales with the working tree rather than the
    39	// session, and nothing reads it back — the attribution summary it fed is a
    40	// separate field that stays.
    41	const promptAttributionsField = "prompt_attributions"
    42	
    43	// OversizedMetadataBlob is one metadata.json blob over the threshold.
    44	type OversizedMetadataBlob struct {
    45		Path   string        // tree path, e.g. "ab/cdef.../0/metadata.json"
    46		Size   int64         // blob size in bytes
    47		Hash   plumbing.Hash // blob hash
    48		Commit plumbing.Hash // the commit that introduced this blob version
    49	}
    50	
    51	// MetadataSizeScan is the read-only half of the oversized-metadata repair: what
    52	// is oversized, where, and what the elected sync remote holds, so the report and
    53	// the fix share one fetch.
    54	type MetadataSizeScan struct {
    55		Threshold  int64
    56		LocalTip   plumbing.Hash // zero when the branch does not exist locally
    57		RemoteName string        // elected checkpoint sync remote; "" when none
    58		// RemoteTip is the remote-tracking tip of the checkpoint branch on
    59		// RemoteName after a refresh. Zero when there is no remote, the remote has
    60		// no such branch, or the refresh failed and no stale tracking ref exists.
    61		RemoteTip plumbing.Hash
    62		// RemoteErr records a failed refresh or an unreadable tracking ref. After a
    63		// failed refresh RemoteTip may still reflect the tracking ref as it was,
    64		// which the force-with-lease push guards against; after an unreadable ref
    65		// the remote fields are cleared and the fix does not push.
    66		RemoteErr error
    67		// RemoteAhead reports that RemoteTip carries commits LocalTip does not.
    68		RemoteAhead  bool
    69		PushDisabled bool
    70		// DedicatedCheckpointRemote reports that the branch is pushed to a
    71		// checkpoint_remote URL rather than to RemoteName; the fix is withheld.
    72		DedicatedCheckpointRemote bool
    73		// Local are oversized blobs reachable from LocalTip; Remote those reachable
    74		// from RemoteTip and not already in Local.
    75		Local  []OversizedMetadataBlob
    76		Remote []OversizedMetadataBlob
    77	}
    78	
    79	// Empty reports whether nothing is oversized on either side.
    80	func (s *MetadataSizeScan) Empty() bool { return len(s.Local) == 0 && len(s.Remote) == 0 }
    81	
    82	// All returns every oversized blob, largest first.
    83	func (s *MetadataSizeScan) All() []OversizedMetadataBlob {
    84		all := make([]OversizedMetadataBlob, 0, len(s.Local)+len(s.Remote))
    85		all = append(all, s.Local...)
    86		all = append(all, s.Remote...)
    87		sort.SliceStable(all, func(i, j int) bool { return all[i].Size > all[j].Size })
    88		return all
    89	}
    90	
    91	// MetadataShrinkResult describes what ShrinkOversizedCheckpointMetadata did.
    92	type MetadataShrinkResult struct {
    93		OldLocalTip plumbing.Hash
    94		NewLocalTip plumbing.Hash
    95		// CommitsRewritten counts commits of the local branch that were rebuilt.
    96		CommitsRewritten int
    97		// RemoteCommitsRewritten counts commits of the remote's history that were
    98		// rebuilt because the remote was ahead of the local branch.
    99		RemoteCommitsRewritten int
   100		BlobsShrunk            int
   101		// StillOversized lists blobs that remain over the threshold after the
   102		// prompt_attributions field was removed — bloat of a kind this repair does
   103		// not know about, reported rather than guessed at.
   104		StillOversized []OversizedMetadataBlob
   105		Pushed         bool
   106		// PushSkippedReason explains a Pushed == false when no error occurred.
   107		PushSkippedReason string
   108	}
   109	
   110	// ScanOversizedCheckpointMetadata refreshes the elected sync remote's tracking
   111	// ref for the checkpoint branch (best effort) and reports every metadata.json
   112	// blob over threshold reachable from the local branch or from that tracking ref.
   113	// It is read-only: nothing under refs/heads is touched.
   114	//
   115	// The remote side matters because the repair force-pushes: a blob that is only
   116	// on the remote (an earlier local repair whose push failed) still blocks the
   117	// mirror, and an ordinary pre-push would replay the local branch onto that
   118	// remote history and reintroduce it.
   119	//
   120	// The network is touched only when something is oversized. The local branch
   121	// and the remote-tracking ref as last fetched are scanned first; when both are
   122	// clean the answer is "OK" without a fetch, which keeps the routine doctor run
   123	// offline. When either shows a problem the tracking ref is refreshed and the
   124	// remote side re-scanned, so the fix that follows works from the remote's
   125	// current tip.
   126	func ScanOversizedCheckpointMetadata(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, remoteName string, threshold int64) (*MetadataSizeScan, error) {
   127		v1 := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName)
   128		scan := &MetadataSizeScan{Threshold: threshold, RemoteName: remoteName}
   129	
   130		localTip, err := readV1Tip(repo, v1)
   131		if err != nil {
   132			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read local %s: %w", v1.Short(), err)
   133		}
   134		scan.LocalTip = localTip
   135		scan.Local, err = findOversizedMetadataBlobs(ctx, repo, localTip, threshold)
   136		if err != nil {
   137			return nil, fmt.Errorf("scan local %s: %w", v1.Short(), err)
   138		}
   139		// The tracking ref as last fetched. An unreadable one (dangling, partial
   140		// clone) is reported, not fatal: doctor's other checks must still run, and
   141		// with a clean local branch there is nothing this check would do anyway.
   142		var trackingRef plumbing.ReferenceName
   143		var readErr error
   144		if remoteName != "" {
   145			trackingRef = plumbing.NewRemoteReferenceName(remoteName, paths.MetadataBranchName)
   146			readErr = scan.readRemoteSide(ctx, repo, trackingRef)
   147		}
   148		if len(scan.Local) == 0 && (remoteName == "" || readErr != nil || len(scan.Remote) == 0) {
   149			scan.RemoteErr = readErr
   150			return scan, nil //nolint:nilerr // fail-soft: the unreadable tracking ref is reported on scan.RemoteErr, not fatal to doctor
   151		}
   152		// Something is oversized (or the stale tracking ref could not tell us).
   153		// Where pre-push actually sends the branch decides what happens next: a
   154		// dedicated checkpoint_remote URL has no remote-tracking ref to lease
   155		// against, and pre-push replays local commits onto whatever that URL
   156		// holds, so a local-only rewrite there would be undone by the next push.
   157		// Report it and stop rather than repair half of it — and decide that
   158		// BEFORE the no-remote early return below, so a repository whose only
   159		// checkpoint destination is the dedicated URL is refused the same way.
   160		// The settings are read directly rather than through resolvePushSettings,
   161		// which may fetch and create the local branch as a side effect; this scan
   162		// must stay read-only. They are read for THIS repository's worktree, not
   163		// the process working directory: the scan is handed a repo and must not
   164		// answer for whichever checkout the caller happens to be standing in.
   165		if s, loadErr := loadSettingsForRepo(ctx, repo); loadErr == nil {
   166			scan.PushDisabled = s.IsPushSessionsDisabled()
   167			if s.GetCheckpointRemote() != nil {
   168				scan.DedicatedCheckpointRemote = true
   169				scan.clearRemote()
   170				return scan, nil
   171			}
   172		} else {
   173			// Unknown push policy: do not push. The local rewrite is still useful.
   174			scan.PushDisabled = true
   175		}
   176		if remoteName == "" {
   177			return scan, nil
   178		}
   179		// Refresh from the remote so the fix works from its current tip.
   180		if fetchErr := refreshCheckpointTrackingRef(ctx, remoteName, v1, trackingRef); fetchErr != nil {
   181			scan.RemoteErr = fetchErr
   182		}
   183		if err := scan.readRemoteSide(ctx, repo, trackingRef); err != nil {
   184			scan.RemoteErr = errors.Join(scan.RemoteErr, err)
   185			scan.clearRemote()
   186		}
   187		return scan, nil
   188	}
   189	
   190	// ErrDedicatedCheckpointRemote reports that the repository pushes its
   191	// checkpoint branch to a dedicated checkpoint_remote URL, which the automatic
   192	// repair does not handle (see ScanOversizedCheckpointMetadata).
   193	var ErrDedicatedCheckpointRemote = errors.New("checkpoint branch is pushed to a dedicated checkpoint remote; automatic repair is not available there")
   194	
   195	// loadSettingsForRepo reads Entire settings for the worktree repo was opened on.
   196	func loadSettingsForRepo(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository) (*settings.EntireSettings, error) {
   197		wt, err := repo.Worktree()
   198		if err != nil {
   199			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve worktree: %w", err)
   200		}
   201		return settings.LoadForWorktreeRoot(ctx, wt.Filesystem().Root()) //nolint:wrapcheck // settings errors carry their own context
   202	}
   203	
   204	// clearRemote leaves the scan with no knowledge of the remote side.
   205	func (s *MetadataSizeScan) clearRemote() {
   206		s.RemoteTip = plumbing.ZeroHash
   207		s.RemoteAhead = false
   208		s.Remote = nil
   209	}
   210	
   211	// readRemoteSide fills RemoteTip, RemoteAhead and Remote from the tracking
   212	// ref as it currently stands. On error the remote fields are cleared.
   213	func (s *MetadataSizeScan) readRemoteSide(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, trackingRef plumbing.ReferenceName) (err error) {
   214		defer func() {
   215			if err != nil {
   216				s.clearRemote()
   217			}
   218		}()
   219		remoteTip, err := readV1Tip(repo, trackingRef)
   220		if err != nil {
   221			return fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", trackingRef.Short(), err)
   222		}
   223		s.RemoteTip = remoteTip
   224		s.RemoteAhead = false
   225		s.Remote = nil
   226		switch {
   227		case remoteTip.IsZero():
   228			return nil
   229		case s.LocalTip.IsZero():
   230			s.RemoteAhead = true
   231		case !remoteTip.Equal(s.LocalTip):
   232			base, mbErr := computeMergeBase(repo, s.LocalTip, remoteTip)
   233			if mbErr != nil {
   234				return fmt.Errorf("compare local and %s: %w", trackingRef.Short(), mbErr)
   235			}
   236			s.RemoteAhead = !base.Equal(remoteTip)
   237		}
   238		if remoteTip.Equal(s.LocalTip) {
   239			return nil
   240		}
   241		remoteBlobs, err := findOversizedMetadataBlobs(ctx, repo, remoteTip, s.Threshold)
   242		if err != nil {
   243			return fmt.Errorf("scan %s: %w", trackingRef.Short(), err)
   244		}
   245		seen := make(map[plumbing.Hash]struct{}, len(s.Local))
   246		for _, b := range s.Local {
   247			seen[b.Hash] = struct{}{}
   248		}
   249		for _, b := range remoteBlobs {
   250			if _, dup := seen[b.Hash]; !dup {
   251				s.Remote = append(s.Remote, b)
   252			}
   253		}
   254		return nil
   255	}
   256	
   257	// refreshCheckpointTrackingRef fetches the checkpoint branch from remoteName
   258	// into its remote-tracking ref. A remote that has no such branch is not an
   259	// error: the tracking ref is simply left as it was (normally absent).
   260	func refreshCheckpointTrackingRef(ctx context.Context, remoteName string, branch, trackingRef plumbing.ReferenceName) error {
   261		fetchCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, checkpointRemoteForegroundFetchTimeout)
   262		defer cancel()
   263		output, err := remote.Fetch(fetchCtx, remote.FetchOptions{
   264			Remote:   remoteName,
   265			RefSpecs: []string{"+" + branch.String() + ":" + trackingRef.String()},
   266			NoTags:   true,
   267			NoFilter: true, // the scan reads blob sizes, which a blob-filtered fetch would not have
   268		})
   269		if err == nil {
   270			return nil
   271		}
   272		if strings.Contains(string(output), "couldn't find remote ref") {
   273			return nil
   274		}
   275		if msg := strings.TrimSpace(string(output)); msg != "" {
   276			return fmt.Errorf("fetch %s from %s: %s: %w", branch.Short(), remoteName, msg, err)
   277		}
   278		return fmt.Errorf("fetch %s from %s: %w", branch.Short(), remoteName, err)
   279	}
   280	
   281	// findOversizedMetadataBlobs walks the history behind tip and returns every
   282	// metadata.json blob larger than threshold, largest first. Each commit is
   283	// diffed against its first parent, so the walk costs the size of the changes
   284	// rather than the size of the (cumulative) trees; the root commit's tree is
   285	// listed in full.
   286	func findOversizedMetadataBlobs(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, tip plumbing.Hash, threshold int64) ([]OversizedMetadataBlob, error) {
   287		if tip.IsZero() {
   288			return nil, nil
   289		}
   290		iter, err := repo.Log(&git.LogOptions{From: tip})
   291		if err != nil {
   292			return nil, fmt.Errorf("log %s: %w", tip, err)
   293		}
   294		defer iter.Close()
   295	
   296		seen := make(map[plumbing.Hash]struct{})
   297		var found []OversizedMetadataBlob
   298		walkErr := iter.ForEach(func(c *object.Commit) error {
   299			if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
   300				return ctxErr //nolint:wrapcheck // context cancellation propagates as-is
   301			}
   302			return forEachMetadataBlobIntroduced(ctx, c, func(blobPath string, hash plumbing.Hash) error {
   303				if _, dup := seen[hash]; dup {
   304					return nil
   305				}
   306				seen[hash] = struct{}{}
   307				blob, blobErr := repo.BlobObject(hash)
   308				if blobErr != nil {
   309					return fmt.Errorf("blob %s at %s: %w", hash, blobPath, blobErr)
   310				}
   311				if blob.Size > threshold {
   312					found = append(found, OversizedMetadataBlob{Path: blobPath, Size: blob.Size, Hash: hash, Commit: c.Hash})
   313				}
   314				return nil
   315			})
   316		})
   317		if walkErr != nil {
   318			return nil, fmt.Errorf("walk history of %s: %w", tip, walkErr)
   319		}
   320		sort.SliceStable(found, func(i, j int) bool { return found[i].Size > found[j].Size })
   321		return found, nil
   322	}
   323	
   324	// forEachMetadataBlobIntroduced calls fn for every metadata.json blob that
   325	// commit c adds or changes relative to any of its parents. The checkpoint
   326	// branch is linear in practice, but a merge is diffed against every parent so
   327	// a blob that arrived through a side parent is not missed; the caller dedupes
   328	// by hash, so over-reporting costs nothing.
   329	func forEachMetadataBlobIntroduced(ctx context.Context, c *object.Commit, fn func(blobPath string, hash plumbing.Hash) error) error {
   330		tree, err := c.Tree()
   331		if err != nil {
   332			return fmt.Errorf("tree of %s: %w", c.Hash, err)
   333		}
   334		if c.NumParents() == 0 {
   335			files := tree.Files()
   336			defer files.Close()
   337			return files.ForEach(func(f *object.File) error { //nolint:wrapcheck // fn's errors carry their own context
   338				if path.Base(f.Name) != paths.MetadataFileName {
   339					return nil
   340				}
   341				return fn(f.Name, f.Hash)
   342			})
   343		}
   344		for i := range c.NumParents() {
   345			parent, err := c.Parent(i)
   346			if err != nil {
   347				return fmt.Errorf("parent %d of %s: %w", i, c.Hash, err)
   348			}
   349			parentTree, err := parent.Tree()
   350			if err != nil {
   351				return fmt.Errorf("tree of %s: %w", parent.Hash, err)
   352			}

    30	// MetadataRelation classifies how the local primary metadata ref stands relative

    38		// nothing to relate.

    40		// MetadataRelationAligned: identical tips.

    45		// fetch fast-forwards.

    63	// remoteRefName. Pure read — it never writes a ref, and it runs exactly one

    65	func CompareMetadataWithRemote(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, remoteRefName plumbing.ReferenceName) (MetadataComparison, error) {

    71			return c, nil

    74			return c, fmt.Errorf("failed to check local primary metadata ref: %w", err)
    75		}

    77		if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
    78			return c, nil
    79		}
    80		if err != nil {
    81			return c, fmt.Errorf("failed to check remote metadata ref: %w", err)
    82		}

    84		c.Local, c.Remote = localRef.Hash(), remoteRef.Hash()
    85		if c.Local == c.Remote {
    86			c.Relation = MetadataRelationAligned

    91		if err != nil {

   216		}

   219		}

   227		}

   238		}

   240			// Shared ancestry (diverged or ancestor) — not our problem
   241			return nil
   242		}
   243	
   244		// Disconnected — cherry-pick local commits onto remote tip
   245		fmt.Fprintln(w, "[entire] Detected disconnected session metadata (local and remote share no common ancestor)")

   247		shallow, err := loadShallowHashes(ctx, repoPath)
   248		if err != nil {

   250		}

   294	// isDisconnected checks if two commits have no common ancestor using git merge-base.
   295	// Returns (true, nil) if disconnected, (false, nil) if they share ancestry,
   296	// or (false, error) if git merge-base failed for another reason.
   297	//
   298	// git merge-base exit codes:
   299	//   - 0: common ancestor found (shared ancestry)
   300	//   - 1: no common ancestor (disconnected)
   301	//   - 128+: error (corrupt repo, invalid hash, etc.)
   302	func isDisconnected(ctx context.Context, repoPath, hashA, hashB string) (bool, error) {
   303		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
   304		defer cancel()
   305		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "merge-base", hashA, hashB)
   306		cmd.Dir = repoPath

   308			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
   309			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) && exitErr.ExitCode() == 1 {
   310				return true, nil // No common ancestor — disconnected
   311			}
   312			return false, fmt.Errorf("git merge-base failed: %w", err)
   313		}
   314		return false, nil // Shared ancestry
   315	}

   317	// collectCommitChain walks from tip to root following first parent, returns oldest-first.
   318	// Commits listed in shallow are treated as roots — the walk stops at them without
   319	// traversing into their parents. go-git's repo.CommitObject().ParentHashes does not
   320	// consult .git/shallow on its own, so without this check the walk would stroll past
   321	// shallow boundaries into stale objects left in the pack (e.g., when the remote
   322	// branch has been rebuilt since the last full fetch), producing a phantom chain of
   323	// commits that no longer represent the actual checkpoint history.
   324	func collectCommitChain(repo *git.Repository, tip plumbing.Hash, shallow map[plumbing.Hash]bool) ([]*object.Commit, error) {
   325		var chain []*object.Commit
   326		current := tip
   327	
   328		reachedRoot := false
   329		for range MaxCommitTraversalDepth {
   330			commit, err := repo.CommitObject(current)
   331			if err != nil {
   332				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit %s: %w", current, err)
   333			}
   334			chain = append(chain, commit)
   335	
   336			if len(commit.ParentHashes) == 0 {
   337				reachedRoot = true
   338				break
   339			}
   340			if shallow[current] {
   341				// Shallow boundary — treat as a root.
   342				reachedRoot = true
   343				break
   344			}
   345			current = commit.ParentHashes[0]
   346		}
   347	
   348		if !reachedRoot {
   349			return nil, fmt.Errorf("commit chain exceeded %d commits without reaching root; aborting reconciliation", MaxCommitTraversalDepth)
   350		}
   351	
   352		// Reverse to oldest-first
   353		for i, j := 0, len(chain)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
   354			chain[i], chain[j] = chain[j], chain[i]
   355		}
   356	
   357		return chain, nil
   358	}

   360	// loadShallowHashes returns the commit hashes listed in the repository's
   361	// shallow file, or an empty map if the repository is not shallow.
   362	func loadShallowHashes(ctx context.Context, repoPath string) (map[plumbing.Hash]bool, error) {
   363		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
   364		cmd.Dir = repoPath
   365		out, err := cmd.Output()
   366		if err != nil {
   367			return nil, fmt.Errorf("git rev-parse --git-common-dir: %w", err)
   368		}
   369		gitDir := strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
   370		if !filepath.IsAbs(gitDir) {
   371			gitDir = filepath.Join(repoPath, gitDir)
   372		}
   373		// Through the common dir's root like every other read there. "shallow" is a
   374		// fixed name and gitDir came from git's own --git-common-dir, so nothing here
   375		// can traverse today; the root is what keeps that true without depending on
   376		// it, and it shares the one handle per clone.
   377		root, err := gitdir.OpenAt(gitDir)
   378		if err != nil {
   379			return nil, fmt.Errorf("open git common dir: %w", err)
   380		}
   381		data, err := osroot.ReadFileNoFollow(root, "shallow")
   382		if err != nil {
   383			if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
   384				return map[plumbing.Hash]bool{}, nil
   385			}
   386			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read shallow file: %w", err)
   387		}
   388		set := map[plumbing.Hash]bool{}
   389		for _, line := range strings.Split(string(data), "\n") {
   390			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
   391			if line == "" {
   392				continue
   393			}
   394			set[plumbing.NewHash(line)] = true
   395		}
   396		return set, nil
   397	}

   399	// cherryPickOnto applies each commit's delta onto base, building a linear chain.
   400	// For each commit, it computes the full diff from its parent (additions, modifications,
   401	// and deletions), then applies that delta onto the current tip's tree.
   402	//
   403	// Commits listed in shallow are treated as roots: their delta is computed against
   404	// an empty tree rather than against their (past-the-boundary) parent. Without this,
   405	// a shallow-boundary commit would be diffed against a stale parent tree whose
   406	// objects live in the local pack but no longer represent the actual checkpoint
   407	// history — producing nonsense changes when replayed onto the remote tip.
   408	func cherryPickOnto(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, base plumbing.Hash, commits []*object.Commit, shallow map[plumbing.Hash]bool) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   409		currentTip := base
   410	
   411		for _, commit := range commits {
   412			changes, err := treeChangesForCherryPick(ctx, repo, commit, shallow)
   413			if err != nil {
   414				return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   415			}
   416			if len(changes) == 0 {
   417				continue // Skip no-op commits
   418			}
   419	
   420			tipCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(currentTip)
   421			if err != nil {
   422				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get tip commit: %w", err)
   423			}
   424	
   425			mergedTreeHash, err := checkpoint.ApplyTreeChanges(ctx, repo, tipCommit.TreeHash, changes)
   426			if err != nil {
   427				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to apply cherry-pick changes: %w", err)
   428			}
   429			if mergedTreeHash.Equal(tipCommit.TreeHash) {
   430				continue
   431			}
   432	
   433			// Create new commit on top of current tip, preserving original message/author
   434			newHash, err := createCherryPickCommit(ctx, repo, mergedTreeHash, currentTip, commit)
   435			if err != nil {
   436				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to create cherry-pick commit: %w", err)
   437			}
   438	
   439			currentTip = newHash
   440		}
   441	
   442		return currentTip, nil
   443	}
   444	
   445	func treeChangesForCherryPick(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, commit *object.Commit, shallow map[plumbing.Hash]bool) ([]checkpoint.TreeChange, error) {
   446		commitTree, err := commit.Tree()
   447		if err != nil {
   448			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get tree for commit %s: %w", commit.Hash, err)
   449		}
   450	
   451		var parentTree *object.Tree
   452		// Shallow-boundary commits are treated as roots — see cherryPickOnto for why.
   453		if len(commit.ParentHashes) > 0 && !shallow[commit.Hash] {
   454			parentCommit, pErr := repo.CommitObject(commit.ParentHashes[0])
   455			if pErr != nil {
   456				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get parent commit %s: %w", commit.ParentHashes[0], pErr)
   457			}
   458			parentTree, err = parentCommit.Tree()
   459			if err != nil {
   460				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get parent tree for commit %s: %w", commit.ParentHashes[0], err)
   461			}
   462		}
   463	
   464		changes, err := object.DiffTreeContext(ctx, parentTree, commitTree)
   465		if err != nil {
   466			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to diff commit %s against parent: %w", commit.Hash, err)
   467		}
   468	
   469		treeChanges := make([]checkpoint.TreeChange, 0, len(changes))
   470		for _, change := range changes {
   471			treeChange, changeErr := changeToTreeChange(change)
   472			if changeErr != nil {
   473				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to convert change in commit %s: %w", commit.Hash, changeErr)
   474			}
   475			treeChanges = append(treeChanges, treeChange)
   476		}
   477		return treeChanges, nil
   478	}
   479	
   480	func changeToTreeChange(change *object.Change) (checkpoint.TreeChange, error) {
   481		action, err := change.Action()
   482		if err != nil {
   483			return checkpoint.TreeChange{}, fmt.Errorf("change action: %w", err)
   484		}
   485	
   486		switch action {
   487		case merkletrie.Insert, merkletrie.Modify:
   488			entry := change.To.TreeEntry
   489			return checkpoint.TreeChange{
   490				Path: change.To.Name,
   491				Entry: &object.TreeEntry{
   492					Name: entry.Name,
   493					Mode: entry.Mode,
   494					Hash: entry.Hash,
   495				},
   496			}, nil
   497		case merkletrie.Delete:
   498			return checkpoint.TreeChange{Path: change.From.Name}, nil
   499		default:
   500			return checkpoint.TreeChange{}, fmt.Errorf("unsupported action %s", action)
   501		}
   502	}
   503	
   504	// createCherryPickCommit creates a new commit on top of parent, preserving the
   505	// original commit's message and author.
   506	func createCherryPickCommit(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, treeHash, parent plumbing.Hash, original *object.Commit) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   507		committerName, committerEmail := GetGitAuthorFromRepo(repo)
   508		now := time.Now()
   509	
   510		commit := &object.Commit{
   511			TreeHash:     treeHash,
   512			ParentHashes: []plumbing.Hash{parent},
   513			Author:       original.Author,
   514			Committer: object.Signature{
   515				Name:  committerName,
   516				Email: committerEmail,
   517				When:  now,
   518			},
   519			Message: original.Message,
   520		}

    27	// OversizedCheckpointMetadataThreshold is the blob size above which a
    28	// per-session metadata.json on entire/checkpoints/v1 is reported by
    29	// `entire doctor`. GitHub warns at 50 MiB and refuses any blob over 100 MiB, and
    30	// a refused blob anywhere in the branch's history makes the whole branch
    31	// unpushable there — including through a forge's push mirror. A healthy
    32	// metadata.json is tens of kilobytes, so anything past this line is the
    33	// pre-v0.10.1 prompt_attributions bloat (see checkpoint.MaxPromptAttributionsBytes),
    34	// not a large session.
    35	const OversizedCheckpointMetadataThreshold int64 = 50 << 20
    36	
    37	// promptAttributionsField is the metadata.json key the shrink removes. It is
    38	// the only field whose size scales with the working tree rather than the
    39	// session, and nothing reads it back — the attribution summary it fed is a
    40	// separate field that stays.
    41	const promptAttributionsField = "prompt_attributions"

    43	// OversizedMetadataBlob is one metadata.json blob over the threshold.
    44	type OversizedMetadataBlob struct {
    45		Path   string        // tree path, e.g. "ab/cdef.../0/metadata.json"
    46		Size   int64         // blob size in bytes
    47		Hash   plumbing.Hash // blob hash
    48		Commit plumbing.Hash // the commit that introduced this blob version

    51	// MetadataSizeScan is the read-only half of the oversized-metadata repair: what
    52	// is oversized, where, and what the elected sync remote holds, so the report and
    53	// the fix share one fetch.
    54	type MetadataSizeScan struct {
    55		Threshold  int64
    56		LocalTip   plumbing.Hash // zero when the branch does not exist locally
    57		RemoteName string        // elected checkpoint sync remote; "" when none
    58		// RemoteTip is the remote-tracking tip of the checkpoint branch on
    59		// RemoteName after a refresh. Zero when there is no remote, the remote has
    60		// no such branch, or the refresh failed and no stale tracking ref exists.
    61		RemoteTip plumbing.Hash
    62		// RemoteErr records a failed refresh or an unreadable tracking ref. After a
    63		// failed refresh RemoteTip may still reflect the tracking ref as it was,
    64		// which the force-with-lease push guards against; after an unreadable ref
    65		// the remote fields are cleared and the fix does not push.
    66		RemoteErr error
    67		// RemoteAhead reports that RemoteTip carries commits LocalTip does not.
    68		RemoteAhead  bool
    69		PushDisabled bool
    70		// DedicatedCheckpointRemote reports that the branch is pushed to a
    71		// checkpoint_remote URL rather than to RemoteName; the fix is withheld.
    72		DedicatedCheckpointRemote bool
    73		// Local are oversized blobs reachable from LocalTip; Remote those reachable
    74		// from RemoteTip and not already in Local.
    75		Local  []OversizedMetadataBlob
    76		Remote []OversizedMetadataBlob
    77	}
    78	
    79	// Empty reports whether nothing is oversized on either side.
    80	func (s *MetadataSizeScan) Empty() bool { return len(s.Local) == 0 && len(s.Remote) == 0 }
    81	
    82	// All returns every oversized blob, largest first.
    83	func (s *MetadataSizeScan) All() []OversizedMetadataBlob {
    84		all := make([]OversizedMetadataBlob, 0, len(s.Local)+len(s.Remote))
    85		all = append(all, s.Local...)
    86		all = append(all, s.Remote...)
    87		sort.SliceStable(all, func(i, j int) bool { return all[i].Size > all[j].Size })
    88		return all
    89	}

   110	// ScanOversizedCheckpointMetadata refreshes the elected sync remote's tracking
   111	// ref for the checkpoint branch (best effort) and reports every metadata.json
   112	// blob over threshold reachable from the local branch or from that tracking ref.
   113	// It is read-only: nothing under refs/heads is touched.
   114	//
   115	// The remote side matters because the repair force-pushes: a blob that is only
   116	// on the remote (an earlier local repair whose push failed) still blocks the
   117	// mirror, and an ordinary pre-push would replay the local branch onto that
   118	// remote history and reintroduce it.
   119	//
   120	// The network is touched only when something is oversized. The local branch
   121	// and the remote-tracking ref as last fetched are scanned first; when both are
   122	// clean the answer is "OK" without a fetch, which keeps the routine doctor run
   123	// offline. When either shows a problem the tracking ref is refreshed and the
   124	// remote side re-scanned, so the fix that follows works from the remote's
   125	// current tip.
   126	func ScanOversizedCheckpointMetadata(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, remoteName string, threshold int64) (*MetadataSizeScan, error) {
   127		v1 := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName)
   128		scan := &MetadataSizeScan{Threshold: threshold, RemoteName: remoteName}
   129	
   130		localTip, err := readV1Tip(repo, v1)
   131		if err != nil {
   132			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read local %s: %w", v1.Short(), err)
   133		}
   134		scan.LocalTip = localTip
   135		scan.Local, err = findOversizedMetadataBlobs(ctx, repo, localTip, threshold)
   136		if err != nil {
   137			return nil, fmt.Errorf("scan local %s: %w", v1.Short(), err)
   138		}
   139		// The tracking ref as last fetched. An unreadable one (dangling, partial
   140		// clone) is reported, not fatal: doctor's other checks must still run, and
   141		// with a clean local branch there is nothing this check would do anyway.
   142		var trackingRef plumbing.ReferenceName
   143		var readErr error
   144		if remoteName != "" {
   145			trackingRef = plumbing.NewRemoteReferenceName(remoteName, paths.MetadataBranchName)
   146			readErr = scan.readRemoteSide(ctx, repo, trackingRef)
   147		}
   148		if len(scan.Local) == 0 && (remoteName == "" || readErr != nil || len(scan.Remote) == 0) {
   149			scan.RemoteErr = readErr
   150			return scan, nil //nolint:nilerr // fail-soft: the unreadable tracking ref is reported on scan.RemoteErr, not fatal to doctor
   151		}
   152		// Something is oversized (or the stale tracking ref could not tell us).
   153		// Where pre-push actually sends the branch decides what happens next: a
   154		// dedicated checkpoint_remote URL has no remote-tracking ref to lease
   155		// against, and pre-push replays local commits onto whatever that URL
   156		// holds, so a local-only rewrite there would be undone by the next push.
   157		// Report it and stop rather than repair half of it — and decide that
   158		// BEFORE the no-remote early return below, so a repository whose only
   159		// checkpoint destination is the dedicated URL is refused the same way.
   160		// The settings are read directly rather than through resolvePushSettings,
   161		// which may fetch and create the local branch as a side effect; this scan
   162		// must stay read-only. They are read for THIS repository's worktree, not
   163		// the process working directory: the scan is handed a repo and must not
   164		// answer for whichever checkout the caller happens to be standing in.
   165		if s, loadErr := loadSettingsForRepo(ctx, repo); loadErr == nil {
   166			scan.PushDisabled = s.IsPushSessionsDisabled()
   167			if s.GetCheckpointRemote() != nil {
   168				scan.DedicatedCheckpointRemote = true
   169				scan.clearRemote()
   170				return scan, nil
   171			}
   172		} else {
   173			// Unknown push policy: do not push. The local rewrite is still useful.
   174			scan.PushDisabled = true
   175		}
   176		if remoteName == "" {
   177			return scan, nil
   178		}
   179		// Refresh from the remote so the fix works from its current tip.
   180		if fetchErr := refreshCheckpointTrackingRef(ctx, remoteName, v1, trackingRef); fetchErr != nil {
   181			scan.RemoteErr = fetchErr
   182		}
   183		if err := scan.readRemoteSide(ctx, repo, trackingRef); err != nil {
   184			scan.RemoteErr = errors.Join(scan.RemoteErr, err)
   185			scan.clearRemote()
   186		}
   187		return scan, nil
   188	}

   191	// checkpoint branch to a dedicated checkpoint_remote URL, which the automatic
   192	// repair does not handle (see ScanOversizedCheckpointMetadata).
   193	var ErrDedicatedCheckpointRemote = errors.New("checkpoint branch is pushed to a dedicated checkpoint remote; automatic repair is not available there")

   195	// loadSettingsForRepo reads Entire settings for the worktree repo was opened on.
   196	func loadSettingsForRepo(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository) (*settings.EntireSettings, error) {

   204	// clearRemote leaves the scan with no knowledge of the remote side.
   205	func (s *MetadataSizeScan) clearRemote() {
   206		s.RemoteTip = plumbing.ZeroHash
   207		s.RemoteAhead = false
   208		s.Remote = nil
   209	}
   210	
   211	// readRemoteSide fills RemoteTip, RemoteAhead and Remote from the tracking
   212	// ref as it currently stands. On error the remote fields are cleared.
   213	func (s *MetadataSizeScan) readRemoteSide(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, trackingRef plumbing.ReferenceName) (err error) {
   214		defer func() {
   215			if err != nil {
   216				s.clearRemote()
   217			}
   218		}()
   219		remoteTip, err := readV1Tip(repo, trackingRef)
   220		if err != nil {
   221			return fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", trackingRef.Short(), err)
   222		}
   223		s.RemoteTip = remoteTip
   224		s.RemoteAhead = false
   225		s.Remote = nil
   226		switch {
   227		case remoteTip.IsZero():
   228			return nil
   229		case s.LocalTip.IsZero():
   230			s.RemoteAhead = true
   231		case !remoteTip.Equal(s.LocalTip):
   232			base, mbErr := computeMergeBase(repo, s.LocalTip, remoteTip)
   233			if mbErr != nil {
   234				return fmt.Errorf("compare local and %s: %w", trackingRef.Short(), mbErr)
   235			}
   236			s.RemoteAhead = !base.Equal(remoteTip)
   237		}
   238		if remoteTip.Equal(s.LocalTip) {
   239			return nil
   240		}
   241		remoteBlobs, err := findOversizedMetadataBlobs(ctx, repo, remoteTip, s.Threshold)
   242		if err != nil {
   243			return fmt.Errorf("scan %s: %w", trackingRef.Short(), err)
   244		}
   245		seen := make(map[plumbing.Hash]struct{}, len(s.Local))
   246		for _, b := range s.Local {
   247			seen[b.Hash] = struct{}{}
   248		}
   249		for _, b := range remoteBlobs {
   250			if _, dup := seen[b.Hash]; !dup {
   251				s.Remote = append(s.Remote, b)
   252			}
   253		}
   254		return nil
   255	}

   257	// refreshCheckpointTrackingRef fetches the checkpoint branch from remoteName
   258	// into its remote-tracking ref. A remote that has no such branch is not an
   259	// error: the tracking ref is simply left as it was (normally absent).
   260	func refreshCheckpointTrackingRef(ctx context.Context, remoteName string, branch, trackingRef plumbing.ReferenceName) error {
   261		fetchCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, checkpointRemoteForegroundFetchTimeout)
   262		defer cancel()
   263		output, err := remote.Fetch(fetchCtx, remote.FetchOptions{
   264			Remote:   remoteName,
   265			RefSpecs: []string{"+" + branch.String() + ":" + trackingRef.String()},
   266			NoTags:   true,
   267			NoFilter: true, // the scan reads blob sizes, which a blob-filtered fetch would not have
   268		})
   269		if err == nil {
   270			return nil
   271		}
   272		if strings.Contains(string(output), "couldn't find remote ref") {
   273			return nil
   274		}
   275		if msg := strings.TrimSpace(string(output)); msg != "" {
   276			return fmt.Errorf("fetch %s from %s: %s: %w", branch.Short(), remoteName, msg, err)
   277		}
   278		return fmt.Errorf("fetch %s from %s: %w", branch.Short(), remoteName, err)
   279	}

   281	// findOversizedMetadataBlobs walks the history behind tip and returns every
   282	// metadata.json blob larger than threshold, largest first. Each commit is
   283	// diffed against its first parent, so the walk costs the size of the changes
   284	// rather than the size of the (cumulative) trees; the root commit's tree is
   285	// listed in full.
   286	func findOversizedMetadataBlobs(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, tip plumbing.Hash, threshold int64) ([]OversizedMetadataBlob, error) {
   287		if tip.IsZero() {
   288			return nil, nil
   289		}
   290		iter, err := repo.Log(&git.LogOptions{From: tip})
   291		if err != nil {
   292			return nil, fmt.Errorf("log %s: %w", tip, err)
   293		}
   294		defer iter.Close()
   295	
   296		seen := make(map[plumbing.Hash]struct{})
   297		var found []OversizedMetadataBlob
   298		walkErr := iter.ForEach(func(c *object.Commit) error {
   299			if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
   300				return ctxErr //nolint:wrapcheck // context cancellation propagates as-is
   301			}
   302			return forEachMetadataBlobIntroduced(ctx, c, func(blobPath string, hash plumbing.Hash) error {
   303				if _, dup := seen[hash]; dup {
   304					return nil
   305				}
   306				seen[hash] = struct{}{}
   307				blob, blobErr := repo.BlobObject(hash)
   308				if blobErr != nil {
   309					return fmt.Errorf("blob %s at %s: %w", hash, blobPath, blobErr)
   310				}
   311				if blob.Size > threshold {
   312					found = append(found, OversizedMetadataBlob{Path: blobPath, Size: blob.Size, Hash: hash, Commit: c.Hash})
   313				}
   314				return nil
   315			})
   316		})
   317		if walkErr != nil {
   318			return nil, fmt.Errorf("walk history of %s: %w", tip, walkErr)
   319		}
   320		sort.SliceStable(found, func(i, j int) bool { return found[i].Size > found[j].Size })
   321		return found, nil
   322	}

    27	// disconnectedOnce ensures the disconnection warning runs at most once per process.
    28	var disconnectedOnce sync.Once //nolint:gochecknoglobals // intentional per-process gate

    30	// MetadataRelation classifies how the local primary metadata ref stands relative
    31	// to a remote-tracking ref. Derived from a single `git merge-base`, so the
    32	// disconnected, fast-forward and diverged verdicts can never disagree — they used
    33	// to be computed by two functions that each shelled out for the same pair.
    34	type MetadataRelation int
    35	
    36	const (
    37		// MetadataRelationAbsent: one of the two refs does not exist, so there is
    38		// nothing to relate.
    39		MetadataRelationAbsent MetadataRelation = iota
    40		// MetadataRelationAligned: identical tips.
    41		MetadataRelationAligned
    42		// MetadataRelationLocalAhead: the remote tip is an ancestor of local.
    43		MetadataRelationLocalAhead
    44		// MetadataRelationRemoteAhead: local is an ancestor of the remote tip, so a
    45		// fetch fast-forwards.
    46		MetadataRelationRemoteAhead
    47		// MetadataRelationDiverged: both sides advanced past their merge base, so a
    48		// fetch from the elected remote replays the local commits onto the remote tip.
    49		MetadataRelationDiverged
    50		// MetadataRelationDisconnected: no merge base at all (the "empty-orphan bug").
    51		MetadataRelationDisconnected
    52	)
    53	
    54	// MetadataComparison is a MetadataRelation together with the tips it was derived
    55	// from. Local and Remote are zero when Relation is MetadataRelationAbsent.
    56	type MetadataComparison struct {
    57		Relation MetadataRelation
    58		Local    plumbing.Hash
    59		Remote   plumbing.Hash
    60	}

    62	// CompareMetadataWithRemote classifies the local primary metadata ref against
    63	// remoteRefName. Pure read — it never writes a ref, and it runs exactly one
    64	// merge-base subprocess.
    65	func CompareMetadataWithRemote(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, remoteRefName plumbing.ReferenceName) (MetadataComparison, error) {
    66		var c MetadataComparison
    67	
    68		refs := checkpoint.ResolveRefs(ctx)
    69		localRef, err := repo.Reference(refs.Primary, true)
    70		if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
    71			return c, nil
    72		}
    73		if err != nil {
    74			return c, fmt.Errorf("failed to check local primary metadata ref: %w", err)
    75		}
    76		remoteRef, err := repo.Reference(remoteRefName, true)
    77		if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
    78			return c, nil
    79		}
    80		if err != nil {
    81			return c, fmt.Errorf("failed to check remote metadata ref: %w", err)
    82		}
    83	
    84		c.Local, c.Remote = localRef.Hash(), remoteRef.Hash()
    85		if c.Local == c.Remote {
    86			c.Relation = MetadataRelationAligned
    87			return c, nil
    88		}
    89	
    90		repoPath, err := getRepoPath(repo)
    91		if err != nil {
    92			return c, err
    93		}
    94		mergeBase, err := getMergeBase(ctx, repoPath, c.Local.String(), c.Remote.String())
    95		switch {
    96		case errors.Is(err, errNoMergeBase):
    97			c.Relation = MetadataRelationDisconnected
    98		case err != nil:
    99			return c, fmt.Errorf("failed to find merge base for %s: %w", refs.Primary, err)
   100		case mergeBase == c.Local:
   101			c.Relation = MetadataRelationRemoteAhead
   102		case mergeBase == c.Remote:
   103			c.Relation = MetadataRelationLocalAhead
   104		default:
   105			c.Relation = MetadataRelationDiverged
   106		}
   107		return c, nil
   108	}

   110	// IsMetadataDisconnected reports whether the local primary metadata ref and the
   111	// provided fetched or remote-tracking ref exist but share no common ancestor.
   112	func IsMetadataDisconnected(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, remoteRefName plumbing.ReferenceName) (bool, error) {
   113		c, err := CompareMetadataWithRemote(ctx, repo, remoteRefName)
   114		if err != nil {
   115			return false, err
   116		}
   117		return c.Relation == MetadataRelationDisconnected, nil
   118	}

   120	// FirstReadCandidateTrackingRef returns the remote name and remote-tracking
   121	// ref of the first checkpoint read candidate (elected sync remote first, then
   122	// the legacy origin tier) whose tracking ref for primary exists locally.
   123	// Pure read; ok is false when no candidate has a tracking ref (or the chain
   124	// is empty).
   125	func FirstReadCandidateTrackingRef(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, primary plumbing.ReferenceName) (string, plumbing.ReferenceName, bool) {
   126		for _, remoteName := range CheckpointReadRemotes(ctx) {
   127			refName := plumbing.NewRemoteReferenceName(remoteName, primary.Short())
   128			if _, err := repo.Reference(refName, true); err == nil {
   129				return remoteName, refName, true
   130			}
   131		}
   132		return "", "", false
   133	}

   135	// WarnIfMetadataDisconnected checks (once per process) whether the metadata
   136	// branch is disconnected and prints a warning to stderr if so. The check runs
   137	// against the first checkpoint read candidate whose remote-tracking ref
   138	// exists (pure read across both tiers).
   139	// It does NOT fix the problem — users are directed to 'entire doctor'.
   140	//
   141	// Takes the caller's context rather than context.Background(): the probe below
   142	// reads git, so a detached context ignored both interrupt cancellation and the
   143	// invocation-scoped remote-read cache, re-shelling out for answers the caller
   144	// already had.
   145	//
   146	// Uses sync.Once, so a transient failure on the first call permanently suppresses
   147	// the warning. This is acceptable because the check is advisory only and
   148	// 'entire doctor' is the authoritative repair path.
   149	func WarnIfMetadataDisconnected(ctx context.Context) {
   150		disconnectedOnce.Do(func() {
   151			repo, err := OpenRepository(ctx)
   152			if err != nil {
   153				logging.Debug(ctx, "metadata disconnection check: could not open repository",
   154					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   155				return
   156			}
   157			defer repo.Close()
   158			refs := checkpoint.ResolveRefs(ctx)
   159			if !refs.PrimaryFetchableFromRemote() {
   160				return // no remote tracks Primary; nothing to disconnect from
   161			}
   162			_, remoteRefName, ok := FirstReadCandidateTrackingRef(ctx, repo, refs.Primary)
   163			if !ok {
   164				return // no candidate has a tracking ref; nothing to disconnect from
   165			}
   166			disconnected, err := IsMetadataDisconnected(ctx, repo, remoteRefName)
   167			if err != nil {
   168				logging.Debug(ctx, "metadata disconnection check failed",
   169					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   170				return
   171			}
   172			if !disconnected {
   173				return
   174			}
   175			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: Local and remote session metadata branches are disconnected.")
   176			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "[entire] Some checkpoints from remote may not be visible. Run 'entire doctor' to fix.")
   177		})
   178	}
   179	
   180	// ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataRef detects and repairs disconnected local/remote
   181	// metadata refs. Disconnected means no common ancestor, which
   182	// only happens due to the empty-orphan bug. Diverged (shared ancestor) is normal
   183	// and handled by the push path.
   184	//
   185	// Repair strategy: cherry-pick local commits onto remote tip, preserving all data.
   186	// Checkpoint shards use unique paths (<id[:2]>/<id[2:]>/), so cherry-picks always
   187	// apply cleanly.
   188	//
   189	// Progress messages are written to w (typically os.Stderr for hooks or
   190	// cmd.ErrOrStderr() for commands).
   191	// The remote ref can be either a remote-tracking ref or a temporary fetched ref.
   192	func ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataRef(
   193		ctx context.Context,
   194		repo *git.Repository,
   195		localRefName plumbing.ReferenceName,
   196		remoteRefName plumbing.ReferenceName,
   197		w io.Writer,
   198	) error {
   199		advance := func(hash plumbing.Hash) error {
   200			return setRefHash(repo, localRefName, hash)
   201		}
   202	
   203		// Check local ref
   204		localRef, err := repo.Reference(localRefName, true)
   205		if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   206			return nil // No local ref — nothing to reconcile
   207		}
   208		if err != nil {
   209			return fmt.Errorf("failed to check local metadata ref: %w", err)
   210		}
   211	
   212		// Check remote-tracking or fetched ref
   213		remoteRef, err := repo.Reference(remoteRefName, true)
   214		if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   215			return nil // No remote ref — nothing to reconcile
   216		}
   217		if err != nil {
   218			return fmt.Errorf("failed to check remote metadata ref: %w", err)
   219		}
   220	
   221		localHash := localRef.Hash()
   222		remoteHash := remoteRef.Hash()
   223	
   224		// Same hash — nothing to do
   225		if localHash == remoteHash {
   226			return nil
   227		}
   228	
   229		// Check if disconnected using git merge-base
   230		repoPath, err := getRepoPath(repo)
   231		if err != nil {
   232			return err
   233		}
   234	
   235		disconnected, err := isDisconnected(ctx, repoPath, localHash.String(), remoteHash.String())
   236		if err != nil {
   237			return fmt.Errorf("failed to check metadata ref ancestry: %w", err)
   238		}
   239		if !disconnected {
   240			// Shared ancestry (diverged or ancestor) — not our problem
   241			return nil
   242		}
   243	
   244		// Disconnected — cherry-pick local commits onto remote tip
   245		fmt.Fprintln(w, "[entire] Detected disconnected session metadata (local and remote share no common ancestor)")
   246	
   247		shallow, err := loadShallowHashes(ctx, repoPath)
   248		if err != nil {
   249			return fmt.Errorf("failed to load shallow boundaries: %w", err)
   250		}
   251	
   252		// Collect local commits oldest-first
   253		localCommits, err := collectCommitChain(repo, localHash, shallow)
   254		if err != nil {
   255			return fmt.Errorf("failed to collect local commits: %w", err)
   256		}
   257	
   258		// Filter out empty-tree commits (the orphan bug commit)
   259		var dataCommits []*object.Commit
   260		for _, c := range localCommits {
   261			tree, treeErr := c.Tree()
   262			if treeErr != nil {
   263				return fmt.Errorf("failed to read tree for commit %s: %w", c.Hash.String()[:7], treeErr)
   264			}
   265			if len(tree.Entries) > 0 {
   266				dataCommits = append(dataCommits, c)
   267			}
   268		}
   269	
   270		if len(dataCommits) == 0 {
   271			// Local only had empty orphan — just point to remote
   272			if err := advance(remoteHash); err != nil {
   273				return fmt.Errorf("failed to reset metadata ref to remote: %w", err)
   274			}
   275			fmt.Fprintln(w, "[entire] Done — local had no checkpoint data, reset to remote")
   276			return nil
   277		}
   278	
   279		fmt.Fprintf(w, "[entire] Cherry-picking %d local checkpoint(s) onto remote...\n", len(dataCommits))
   280	
   281		newTip, err := cherryPickOnto(ctx, repo, remoteHash, dataCommits, shallow)
   282		if err != nil {
   283			return fmt.Errorf("failed to cherry-pick local commits onto remote: %w", err)
   284		}
   285	
   286		if err := advance(newTip); err != nil {
   287			return fmt.Errorf("failed to update metadata ref: %w", err)
   288		}
   289	
   290		fmt.Fprintln(w, "[entire] Done — all local and remote checkpoints preserved")
   291		return nil
   292	}
   293	
   294	// isDisconnected checks if two commits have no common ancestor using git merge-base.
   295	// Returns (true, nil) if disconnected, (false, nil) if they share ancestry,
   296	// or (false, error) if git merge-base failed for another reason.
   297	//
   298	// git merge-base exit codes:
   299	//   - 0: common ancestor found (shared ancestry)
   300	//   - 1: no common ancestor (disconnected)
   301	//   - 128+: error (corrupt repo, invalid hash, etc.)
   302	func isDisconnected(ctx context.Context, repoPath, hashA, hashB string) (bool, error) {
   303		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
   304		defer cancel()
   305		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "merge-base", hashA, hashB)
   306		cmd.Dir = repoPath
   307		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
   308			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
   309			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) && exitErr.ExitCode() == 1 {
   310				return true, nil // No common ancestor — disconnected
   311			}
   312			return false, fmt.Errorf("git merge-base failed: %w", err)
   313		}
   314		return false, nil // Shared ancestry
   315	}
   316	
   317	// collectCommitChain walks from tip to root following first parent, returns oldest-first.
   318	// Commits listed in shallow are treated as roots — the walk stops at them without
   319	// traversing into their parents. go-git's repo.CommitObject().ParentHashes does not
   320	// consult .git/shallow on its own, so without this check the walk would stroll past
   321	// shallow boundaries into stale objects left in the pack (e.g., when the remote
   322	// branch has been rebuilt since the last full fetch), producing a phantom chain of
   323	// commits that no longer represent the actual checkpoint history.
   324	func collectCommitChain(repo *git.Repository, tip plumbing.Hash, shallow map[plumbing.Hash]bool) ([]*object.Commit, error) {
   325		var chain []*object.Commit
   326		current := tip
   327	
   328		reachedRoot := false
   329		for range MaxCommitTraversalDepth {
   330			commit, err := repo.CommitObject(current)
   331			if err != nil {
   332				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit %s: %w", current, err)
   333			}
   334			chain = append(chain, commit)
   335	
   336			if len(commit.ParentHashes) == 0 {
   337				reachedRoot = true
   338				break
   339			}
   340			if shallow[current] {
   341				// Shallow boundary — treat as a root.
   342				reachedRoot = true
   343				break
   344			}
   345			current = commit.ParentHashes[0]
   346		}
   347	
   348		if !reachedRoot {
   349			return nil, fmt.Errorf("commit chain exceeded %d commits without reaching root; aborting reconciliation", MaxCommitTraversalDepth)
   350		}
   351	
   352		// Reverse to oldest-first
   353		for i, j := 0, len(chain)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
   354			chain[i], chain[j] = chain[j], chain[i]
   355		}
   356	
   357		return chain, nil
   358	}
   359	
   360	// loadShallowHashes returns the commit hashes listed in the repository's
   361	// shallow file, or an empty map if the repository is not shallow.
   362	func loadShallowHashes(ctx context.Context, repoPath string) (map[plumbing.Hash]bool, error) {
   363		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
   364		cmd.Dir = repoPath
   365		out, err := cmd.Output()
   366		if err != nil {
   367			return nil, fmt.Errorf("git rev-parse --git-common-dir: %w", err)
   368		}
   369		gitDir := strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
   370		if !filepath.IsAbs(gitDir) {
   371			gitDir = filepath.Join(repoPath, gitDir)
   372		}
   373		// Through the common dir's root like every other read there. "shallow" is a
   374		// fixed name and gitDir came from git's own --git-common-dir, so nothing here
   375		// can traverse today; the root is what keeps that true without depending on
   376		// it, and it shares the one handle per clone.
   377		root, err := gitdir.OpenAt(gitDir)
   378		if err != nil {
   379			return nil, fmt.Errorf("open git common dir: %w", err)
   380		}
   381		data, err := osroot.ReadFileNoFollow(root, "shallow")
   382		if err != nil {
   383			if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
   384				return map[plumbing.Hash]bool{}, nil
   385			}
   386			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read shallow file: %w", err)
   387		}
   388		set := map[plumbing.Hash]bool{}
   389		for _, line := range strings.Split(string(data), "\n") {
   390			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
   391			if line == "" {
   392				continue
   393			}
   394			set[plumbing.NewHash(line)] = true
   395		}
   396		return set, nil
   397	}
   398	
   399	// cherryPickOnto applies each commit's delta onto base, building a linear chain.
   400	// For each commit, it computes the full diff from its parent (additions, modifications,
   401	// and deletions), then applies that delta onto the current tip's tree.
   402	//
   403	// Commits listed in shallow are treated as roots: their delta is computed against
   404	// an empty tree rather than against their (past-the-boundary) parent. Without this,
   405	// a shallow-boundary commit would be diffed against a stale parent tree whose
   406	// objects live in the local pack but no longer represent the actual checkpoint
   407	// history — producing nonsense changes when replayed onto the remote tip.
   408	func cherryPickOnto(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, base plumbing.Hash, commits []*object.Commit, shallow map[plumbing.Hash]bool) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   409		currentTip := base
   410	
   411		for _, commit := range commits {
   412			changes, err := treeChangesForCherryPick(ctx, repo, commit, shallow)
   413			if err != nil {
   414				return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   415			}
   416			if len(changes) == 0 {
   417				continue // Skip no-op commits
   418			}
   419	
   420			tipCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(currentTip)
   421			if err != nil {
   422				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get tip commit: %w", err)
   423			}
   424	
   425			mergedTreeHash, err := checkpoint.ApplyTreeChanges(ctx, repo, tipCommit.TreeHash, changes)
   426			if err != nil {
   427				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to apply cherry-pick changes: %w", err)
   428			}
   429			if mergedTreeHash.Equal(tipCommit.TreeHash) {
   430				continue
   431			}
   432	
   433			// Create new commit on top of current tip, preserving original message/author
   434			newHash, err := createCherryPickCommit(ctx, repo, mergedTreeHash, currentTip, commit)
   435			if err != nil {
   436				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to create cherry-pick commit: %w", err)
   437			}
   438	
   439			currentTip = newHash
   440		}
   441	
   442		return currentTip, nil
   443	}
   444	
   445	func treeChangesForCherryPick(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, commit *object.Commit, shallow map[plumbing.Hash]bool) ([]checkpoint.TreeChange, error) {
   446		commitTree, err := commit.Tree()
   447		if err != nil {
   448			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get tree for commit %s: %w", commit.Hash, err)
   449		}
   450	
   451		var parentTree *object.Tree
   452		// Shallow-boundary commits are treated as roots — see cherryPickOnto for why.
   453		if len(commit.ParentHashes) > 0 && !shallow[commit.Hash] {
   454			parentCommit, pErr := repo.CommitObject(commit.ParentHashes[0])
   455			if pErr != nil {
   456				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get parent commit %s: %w", commit.ParentHashes[0], pErr)
   457			}
   458			parentTree, err = parentCommit.Tree()
   459			if err != nil {
   460				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get parent tree for commit %s: %w", commit.ParentHashes[0], err)
   461			}
   462		}
   463	
   464		changes, err := object.DiffTreeContext(ctx, parentTree, commitTree)
   465		if err != nil {
   466			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to diff commit %s against parent: %w", commit.Hash, err)
   467		}
   468	
   469		treeChanges := make([]checkpoint.TreeChange, 0, len(changes))
   470		for _, change := range changes {
   471			treeChange, changeErr := changeToTreeChange(change)
   472			if changeErr != nil {
   473				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to convert change in commit %s: %w", commit.Hash, changeErr)
   474			}
   475			treeChanges = append(treeChanges, treeChange)
   476		}
   477		return treeChanges, nil
   478	}
   479	
   480	func changeToTreeChange(change *object.Change) (checkpoint.TreeChange, error) {
   481		action, err := change.Action()
   482		if err != nil {
   483			return checkpoint.TreeChange{}, fmt.Errorf("change action: %w", err)
   484		}
   485	
   486		switch action {
   487		case merkletrie.Insert, merkletrie.Modify:
   488			entry := change.To.TreeEntry
   489			return checkpoint.TreeChange{
   490				Path: change.To.Name,
   491				Entry: &object.TreeEntry{
   492					Name: entry.Name,
   493					Mode: entry.Mode,
   494					Hash: entry.Hash,
   495				},
   496			}, nil
   497		case merkletrie.Delete:
   498			return checkpoint.TreeChange{Path: change.From.Name}, nil
   499		default:
   500			return checkpoint.TreeChange{}, fmt.Errorf("unsupported action %s", action)
   501		}
   502	}
   503	
   504	// createCherryPickCommit creates a new commit on top of parent, preserving the
   505	// original commit's message and author.
   506	func createCherryPickCommit(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, treeHash, parent plumbing.Hash, original *object.Commit) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   507		committerName, committerEmail := GetGitAuthorFromRepo(repo)
   508		now := time.Now()
   509	
   510		commit := &object.Commit{
   511			TreeHash:     treeHash,
   512			ParentHashes: []plumbing.Hash{parent},
   513			Author:       original.Author,
   514			Committer: object.Signature{
   515				Name:  committerName,
   516				Email: committerEmail,
   517				When:  now,
   518			},
   519			Message: original.Message,
   520		}

    27	// OversizedCheckpointMetadataThreshold is the blob size above which a
    28	// per-session metadata.json on entire/checkpoints/v1 is reported by
    29	// `entire doctor`. GitHub warns at 50 MiB and refuses any blob over 100 MiB, and
    30	// a refused blob anywhere in the branch's history makes the whole branch
    31	// unpushable there — including through a forge's push mirror. A healthy
    32	// metadata.json is tens of kilobytes, so anything past this line is the
    33	// pre-v0.10.1 prompt_attributions bloat (see checkpoint.MaxPromptAttributionsBytes),
    34	// not a large session.
    35	const OversizedCheckpointMetadataThreshold int64 = 50 << 20
    36	
    37	// promptAttributionsField is the metadata.json key the shrink removes. It is
    38	// the only field whose size scales with the working tree rather than the
    39	// session, and nothing reads it back — the attribution summary it fed is a
    40	// separate field that stays.
    41	const promptAttributionsField = "prompt_attributions"
    42	
    43	// OversizedMetadataBlob is one metadata.json blob over the threshold.
    44	type OversizedMetadataBlob struct {
    45		Path   string        // tree path, e.g. "ab/cdef.../0/metadata.json"
    46		Size   int64         // blob size in bytes
    47		Hash   plumbing.Hash // blob hash
    48		Commit plumbing.Hash // the commit that introduced this blob version
    49	}
    50	
    51	// MetadataSizeScan is the read-only half of the oversized-metadata repair: what
    52	// is oversized, where, and what the elected sync remote holds, so the report and
    53	// the fix share one fetch.
    54	type MetadataSizeScan struct {
    55		Threshold  int64
    56		LocalTip   plumbing.Hash // zero when the branch does not exist locally
    57		RemoteName string        // elected checkpoint sync remote; "" when none
    58		// RemoteTip is the remote-tracking tip of the checkpoint branch on
    59		// RemoteName after a refresh. Zero when there is no remote, the remote has
    60		// no such branch, or the refresh failed and no stale tracking ref exists.
    61		RemoteTip plumbing.Hash
    62		// RemoteErr records a failed refresh or an unreadable tracking ref. After a
    63		// failed refresh RemoteTip may still reflect the tracking ref as it was,
    64		// which the force-with-lease push guards against; after an unreadable ref
    65		// the remote fields are cleared and the fix does not push.
    66		RemoteErr error
    67		// RemoteAhead reports that RemoteTip carries commits LocalTip does not.
    68		RemoteAhead  bool
    69		PushDisabled bool
    70		// DedicatedCheckpointRemote reports that the branch is pushed to a
    71		// checkpoint_remote URL rather than to RemoteName; the fix is withheld.
    72		DedicatedCheckpointRemote bool
    73		// Local are oversized blobs reachable from LocalTip; Remote those reachable
    74		// from RemoteTip and not already in Local.
    75		Local  []OversizedMetadataBlob
    76		Remote []OversizedMetadataBlob
    77	}
    78	
    79	// Empty reports whether nothing is oversized on either side.
    80	func (s *MetadataSizeScan) Empty() bool { return len(s.Local) == 0 && len(s.Remote) == 0 }
    81	
    82	// All returns every oversized blob, largest first.
    83	func (s *MetadataSizeScan) All() []OversizedMetadataBlob {
    84		all := make([]OversizedMetadataBlob, 0, len(s.Local)+len(s.Remote))
    85		all = append(all, s.Local...)
    86		all = append(all, s.Remote...)
    87		sort.SliceStable(all, func(i, j int) bool { return all[i].Size > all[j].Size })
    88		return all
    89	}
    90	
    91	// MetadataShrinkResult describes what ShrinkOversizedCheckpointMetadata did.
    92	type MetadataShrinkResult struct {
    93		OldLocalTip plumbing.Hash
    94		NewLocalTip plumbing.Hash
    95		// CommitsRewritten counts commits of the local branch that were rebuilt.
    96		CommitsRewritten int
    97		// RemoteCommitsRewritten counts commits of the remote's history that were
    98		// rebuilt because the remote was ahead of the local branch.
    99		RemoteCommitsRewritten int
   100		BlobsShrunk            int
   101		// StillOversized lists blobs that remain over the threshold after the
   102		// prompt_attributions field was removed — bloat of a kind this repair does
   103		// not know about, reported rather than guessed at.
   104		StillOversized []OversizedMetadataBlob

   107		PushSkippedReason string

   109	
   110	// ScanOversizedCheckpointMetadata refreshes the elected sync remote's tracking
   111	// ref for the checkpoint branch (best effort) and reports every metadata.json
   112	// blob over threshold reachable from the local branch or from that tracking ref.
   113	// It is read-only: nothing under refs/heads is touched.
   114	//
   115	// The remote side matters because the repair force-pushes: a blob that is only
   116	// on the remote (an earlier local repair whose push failed) still blocks the
   117	// mirror, and an ordinary pre-push would replay the local branch onto that
   118	// remote history and reintroduce it.
   119	//
   120	// The network is touched only when something is oversized. The local branch
   121	// and the remote-tracking ref as last fetched are scanned first; when both are
   122	// clean the answer is "OK" without a fetch, which keeps the routine doctor run
   123	// offline. When either shows a problem the tracking ref is refreshed and the
   124	// remote side re-scanned, so the fix that follows works from the remote's
   125	// current tip.
   126	func ScanOversizedCheckpointMetadata(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, remoteName string, threshold int64) (*MetadataSizeScan, error) {
   127		v1 := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName)
   128		scan := &MetadataSizeScan{Threshold: threshold, RemoteName: remoteName}
   129	
   130		localTip, err := readV1Tip(repo, v1)
   131		if err != nil {
   132			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read local %s: %w", v1.Short(), err)
   133		}
   134		scan.LocalTip = localTip
   135		scan.Local, err = findOversizedMetadataBlobs(ctx, repo, localTip, threshold)
   136		if err != nil {
   137			return nil, fmt.Errorf("scan local %s: %w", v1.Short(), err)
   138		}
   139		// The tracking ref as last fetched. An unreadable one (dangling, partial
   140		// clone) is reported, not fatal: doctor's other checks must still run, and
   141		// with a clean local branch there is nothing this check would do anyway.
   142		var trackingRef plumbing.ReferenceName
   143		var readErr error
   144		if remoteName != "" {
   145			trackingRef = plumbing.NewRemoteReferenceName(remoteName, paths.MetadataBranchName)
   146			readErr = scan.readRemoteSide(ctx, repo, trackingRef)
   147		}
   148		if len(scan.Local) == 0 && (remoteName == "" || readErr != nil || len(scan.Remote) == 0) {
   149			scan.RemoteErr = readErr
   150			return scan, nil //nolint:nilerr // fail-soft: the unreadable tracking ref is reported on scan.RemoteErr, not fatal to doctor
   151		}
   152		// Something is oversized (or the stale tracking ref could not tell us).
   153		// Where pre-push actually sends the branch decides what happens next: a
   154		// dedicated checkpoint_remote URL has no remote-tracking ref to lease
   155		// against, and pre-push replays local commits onto whatever that URL
   156		// holds, so a local-only rewrite there would be undone by the next push.
   157		// Report it and stop rather than repair half of it — and decide that
   158		// BEFORE the no-remote early return below, so a repository whose only
   159		// checkpoint destination is the dedicated URL is refused the same way.
   160		// The settings are read directly rather than through resolvePushSettings,
   161		// which may fetch and create the local branch as a side effect; this scan
   162		// must stay read-only. They are read for THIS repository's worktree, not
   163		// the process working directory: the scan is handed a repo and must not
   164		// answer for whichever checkout the caller happens to be standing in.
   165		if s, loadErr := loadSettingsForRepo(ctx, repo); loadErr == nil {
   166			scan.PushDisabled = s.IsPushSessionsDisabled()

   174			scan.PushDisabled = true

   178		}

   180		if fetchErr := refreshCheckpointTrackingRef(ctx, remoteName, v1, trackingRef); fetchErr != nil {

   184			scan.RemoteErr = errors.Join(scan.RemoteErr, err)

   211	// readRemoteSide fills RemoteTip, RemoteAhead and Remote from the tracking
   212	// ref as it currently stands. On error the remote fields are cleared.
   213	func (s *MetadataSizeScan) readRemoteSide(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, trackingRef plumbing.ReferenceName) (err error) {
   214		defer func() {
   215			if err != nil {
   216				s.clearRemote()
   217			}
   218		}()
   219		remoteTip, err := readV1Tip(repo, trackingRef)
   220		if err != nil {
   221			return fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", trackingRef.Short(), err)
   222		}
   223		s.RemoteTip = remoteTip
   224		s.RemoteAhead = false
   225		s.Remote = nil
   226		switch {
   227		case remoteTip.IsZero():
   228			return nil
   229		case s.LocalTip.IsZero():
   230			s.RemoteAhead = true
   231		case !remoteTip.Equal(s.LocalTip):
   232			base, mbErr := computeMergeBase(repo, s.LocalTip, remoteTip)
   233			if mbErr != nil {
   234				return fmt.Errorf("compare local and %s: %w", trackingRef.Short(), mbErr)
   235			}
   236			s.RemoteAhead = !base.Equal(remoteTip)
   237		}
   238		if remoteTip.Equal(s.LocalTip) {
   239			return nil
   240		}
   241		remoteBlobs, err := findOversizedMetadataBlobs(ctx, repo, remoteTip, s.Threshold)
   242		if err != nil {
   243			return fmt.Errorf("scan %s: %w", trackingRef.Short(), err)
   244		}
   245		seen := make(map[plumbing.Hash]struct{}, len(s.Local))
   246		for _, b := range s.Local {
   247			seen[b.Hash] = struct{}{}
   248		}
   249		for _, b := range remoteBlobs {
   250			if _, dup := seen[b.Hash]; !dup {
   251				s.Remote = append(s.Remote, b)
   252			}
   253		}
   254		return nil
   255	}

   257	// refreshCheckpointTrackingRef fetches the checkpoint branch from remoteName
   258	// into its remote-tracking ref. A remote that has no such branch is not an
   259	// error: the tracking ref is simply left as it was (normally absent).
   260	func refreshCheckpointTrackingRef(ctx context.Context, remoteName string, branch, trackingRef plumbing.ReferenceName) error {
   261		fetchCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, checkpointRemoteForegroundFetchTimeout)
   262		defer cancel()
   263		output, err := remote.Fetch(fetchCtx, remote.FetchOptions{
   264			Remote:   remoteName,
   265			RefSpecs: []string{"+" + branch.String() + ":" + trackingRef.String()},
   266			NoTags:   true,
   267			NoFilter: true, // the scan reads blob sizes, which a blob-filtered fetch would not have
   268		})
   269		if err == nil {
   270			return nil
   271		}
   272		if strings.Contains(string(output), "couldn't find remote ref") {
   273			return nil
   274		}
   275		if msg := strings.TrimSpace(string(output)); msg != "" {
   276			return fmt.Errorf("fetch %s from %s: %s: %w", branch.Short(), remoteName, msg, err)
   277		}
   278		return fmt.Errorf("fetch %s from %s: %w", branch.Short(), remoteName, err)
   279	}

   281	// findOversizedMetadataBlobs walks the history behind tip and returns every
   282	// metadata.json blob larger than threshold, largest first. Each commit is
   283	// diffed against its first parent, so the walk costs the size of the changes
   284	// rather than the size of the (cumulative) trees; the root commit's tree is
   285	// listed in full.
   286	func findOversizedMetadataBlobs(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, tip plumbing.Hash, threshold int64) ([]OversizedMetadataBlob, error) {
   287		if tip.IsZero() {
   288			return nil, nil
   289		}
   290		iter, err := repo.Log(&git.LogOptions{From: tip})
   291		if err != nil {
   292			return nil, fmt.Errorf("log %s: %w", tip, err)
   293		}
   294		defer iter.Close()
   295	
   296		seen := make(map[plumbing.Hash]struct{})
   297		var found []OversizedMetadataBlob
   298		walkErr := iter.ForEach(func(c *object.Commit) error {
   299			if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
   300				return ctxErr //nolint:wrapcheck // context cancellation propagates as-is
   301			}
   302			return forEachMetadataBlobIntroduced(ctx, c, func(blobPath string, hash plumbing.Hash) error {
   303				if _, dup := seen[hash]; dup {
   304					return nil
   305				}
   306				seen[hash] = struct{}{}
   307				blob, blobErr := repo.BlobObject(hash)
   308				if blobErr != nil {
   309					return fmt.Errorf("blob %s at %s: %w", hash, blobPath, blobErr)
   310				}
   311				if blob.Size > threshold {
   312					found = append(found, OversizedMetadataBlob{Path: blobPath, Size: blob.Size, Hash: hash, Commit: c.Hash})
   313				}
   314				return nil
   315			})
   316		})
   317		if walkErr != nil {
   318			return nil, fmt.Errorf("walk history of %s: %w", tip, walkErr)
   319		}
   320		sort.SliceStable(found, func(i, j int) bool { return found[i].Size > found[j].Size })
   321		return found, nil
   322	}

    30	// MetadataRelation classifies how the local primary metadata ref stands relative
    31	// to a remote-tracking ref. Derived from a single `git merge-base`, so the
    32	// disconnected, fast-forward and diverged verdicts can never disagree — they used
    33	// to be computed by two functions that each shelled out for the same pair.
    34	type MetadataRelation int
    35	
    36	const (
    37		// MetadataRelationAbsent: one of the two refs does not exist, so there is
    38		// nothing to relate.
    39		MetadataRelationAbsent MetadataRelation = iota
    40		// MetadataRelationAligned: identical tips.
    41		MetadataRelationAligned
    42		// MetadataRelationLocalAhead: the remote tip is an ancestor of local.
    43		MetadataRelationLocalAhead
    44		// MetadataRelationRemoteAhead: local is an ancestor of the remote tip, so a
    45		// fetch fast-forwards.
    46		MetadataRelationRemoteAhead
    47		// MetadataRelationDiverged: both sides advanced past their merge base, so a
    48		// fetch from the elected remote replays the local commits onto the remote tip.
    49		MetadataRelationDiverged
    50		// MetadataRelationDisconnected: no merge base at all (the "empty-orphan bug").
    51		MetadataRelationDisconnected
    52	)
    53	
    54	// MetadataComparison is a MetadataRelation together with the tips it was derived
    55	// from. Local and Remote are zero when Relation is MetadataRelationAbsent.
    56	type MetadataComparison struct {
    57		Relation MetadataRelation
    58		Local    plumbing.Hash
    59		Remote   plumbing.Hash
    60	}

    62	// CompareMetadataWithRemote classifies the local primary metadata ref against
    63	// remoteRefName. Pure read — it never writes a ref, and it runs exactly one
    64	// merge-base subprocess.
    65	func CompareMetadataWithRemote(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, remoteRefName plumbing.ReferenceName) (MetadataComparison, error) {
    66		var c MetadataComparison
    67	
    68		refs := checkpoint.ResolveRefs(ctx)
    69		localRef, err := repo.Reference(refs.Primary, true)
    70		if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
    71			return c, nil
    72		}
    73		if err != nil {
    74			return c, fmt.Errorf("failed to check local primary metadata ref: %w", err)
    75		}
    76		remoteRef, err := repo.Reference(remoteRefName, true)
    77		if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
    78			return c, nil
    79		}
    80		if err != nil {
    81			return c, fmt.Errorf("failed to check remote metadata ref: %w", err)
    82		}
    83	
    84		c.Local, c.Remote = localRef.Hash(), remoteRef.Hash()
    85		if c.Local == c.Remote {
    86			c.Relation = MetadataRelationAligned
    87			return c, nil
    88		}
    89	
    90		repoPath, err := getRepoPath(repo)
    91		if err != nil {
    92			return c, err
    93		}
    94		mergeBase, err := getMergeBase(ctx, repoPath, c.Local.String(), c.Remote.String())
    95		switch {
    96		case errors.Is(err, errNoMergeBase):
    97			c.Relation = MetadataRelationDisconnected
    98		case err != nil:
    99			return c, fmt.Errorf("failed to find merge base for %s: %w", refs.Primary, err)
   100		case mergeBase == c.Local:
   101			c.Relation = MetadataRelationRemoteAhead
   102		case mergeBase == c.Remote:
   103			c.Relation = MetadataRelationLocalAhead
   104		default:
   105			c.Relation = MetadataRelationDiverged
   106		}
   107		return c, nil
   108	}

   110	// IsMetadataDisconnected reports whether the local primary metadata ref and the
   111	// provided fetched or remote-tracking ref exist but share no common ancestor.
   112	func IsMetadataDisconnected(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, remoteRefName plumbing.ReferenceName) (bool, error) {
   113		c, err := CompareMetadataWithRemote(ctx, repo, remoteRefName)
   114		if err != nil {
   115			return false, err
   116		}
   117		return c.Relation == MetadataRelationDisconnected, nil
   118	}
