   120	// FirstReadCandidateTrackingRef returns the remote name and remote-tracking
   121	// ref of the first checkpoint read candidate (elected sync remote first, then
   122	// the legacy origin tier) whose tracking ref for primary exists locally.
   123	// Pure read; ok is false when no candidate has a tracking ref (or the chain
   124	// is empty).
   125	func FirstReadCandidateTrackingRef(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, primary plumbing.ReferenceName) (string, plumbing.ReferenceName, bool) {
   126		for _, remoteName := range CheckpointReadRemotes(ctx) {
   127			refName := plumbing.NewRemoteReferenceName(remoteName, primary.Short())
   128			if _, err := repo.Reference(refName, true); err == nil {
   129				return remoteName, refName, true
   130			}
   131		}
   132		return "", "", false
   133	}

   135	// WarnIfMetadataDisconnected checks (once per process) whether the metadata
   136	// branch is disconnected and prints a warning to stderr if so. The check runs
   137	// against the first checkpoint read candidate whose remote-tracking ref
   138	// exists (pure read across both tiers).
   139	// It does NOT fix the problem — users are directed to 'entire doctor'.
   140	//
   141	// Takes the caller's context rather than context.Background(): the probe below
   142	// reads git, so a detached context ignored both interrupt cancellation and the
   143	// invocation-scoped remote-read cache, re-shelling out for answers the caller
   144	// already had.
   145	//
   146	// Uses sync.Once, so a transient failure on the first call permanently suppresses
   147	// the warning. This is acceptable because the check is advisory only and
   148	// 'entire doctor' is the authoritative repair path.
   149	func WarnIfMetadataDisconnected(ctx context.Context) {
   150		disconnectedOnce.Do(func() {
   151			repo, err := OpenRepository(ctx)
   152			if err != nil {
   153				logging.Debug(ctx, "metadata disconnection check: could not open repository",
   154					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   155				return
   156			}
   157			defer repo.Close()
   158			refs := checkpoint.ResolveRefs(ctx)
   159			if !refs.PrimaryFetchableFromRemote() {
   160				return // no remote tracks Primary; nothing to disconnect from
   161			}
   162			_, remoteRefName, ok := FirstReadCandidateTrackingRef(ctx, repo, refs.Primary)
   163			if !ok {
   164				return // no candidate has a tracking ref; nothing to disconnect from
   165			}
   166			disconnected, err := IsMetadataDisconnected(ctx, repo, remoteRefName)
   167			if err != nil {
   168				logging.Debug(ctx, "metadata disconnection check failed",
   169					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   170				return
   171			}
   172			if !disconnected {
   173				return
   174			}
   175			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: Local and remote session metadata branches are disconnected.")
   176			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "[entire] Some checkpoints from remote may not be visible. Run 'entire doctor' to fix.")
   177		})
   178	}

   180	// ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataRef detects and repairs disconnected local/remote
   181	// metadata refs. Disconnected means no common ancestor, which
   182	// only happens due to the empty-orphan bug. Diverged (shared ancestor) is normal
   183	// and handled by the push path.
   184	//
   185	// Repair strategy: cherry-pick local commits onto remote tip, preserving all data.
   186	// Checkpoint shards use unique paths (<id[:2]>/<id[2:]>/), so cherry-picks always
   187	// apply cleanly.
   188	//
   189	// Progress messages are written to w (typically os.Stderr for hooks or
   190	// cmd.ErrOrStderr() for commands).
   191	// The remote ref can be either a remote-tracking ref or a temporary fetched ref.
   192	func ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataRef(
   193		ctx context.Context,
   194		repo *git.Repository,
   195		localRefName plumbing.ReferenceName,
   196		remoteRefName plumbing.ReferenceName,
   197		w io.Writer,
   198	) error {
   199		advance := func(hash plumbing.Hash) error {
   200			return setRefHash(repo, localRefName, hash)
   201		}
   202	
   203		// Check local ref
   204		localRef, err := repo.Reference(localRefName, true)
   205		if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   206			return nil // No local ref — nothing to reconcile
   207		}
   208		if err != nil {
   209			return fmt.Errorf("failed to check local metadata ref: %w", err)
   210		}
   211	
   212		// Check remote-tracking or fetched ref
   213		remoteRef, err := repo.Reference(remoteRefName, true)
   214		if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   215			return nil // No remote ref — nothing to reconcile
   216		}
   217		if err != nil {
   218			return fmt.Errorf("failed to check remote metadata ref: %w", err)
   219		}
   220	
   221		localHash := localRef.Hash()
   222		remoteHash := remoteRef.Hash()
   223	
   224		// Same hash — nothing to do
   225		if localHash == remoteHash {
   226			return nil
   227		}
   228	
   229		// Check if disconnected using git merge-base
   230		repoPath, err := getRepoPath(repo)
   231		if err != nil {
   232			return err
   233		}
   234	
   235		disconnected, err := isDisconnected(ctx, repoPath, localHash.String(), remoteHash.String())
   236		if err != nil {
   237			return fmt.Errorf("failed to check metadata ref ancestry: %w", err)
   238		}
   239		if !disconnected {
   240			// Shared ancestry (diverged or ancestor) — not our problem
   241			return nil
   242		}
   243	
   244		// Disconnected — cherry-pick local commits onto remote tip
   245		fmt.Fprintln(w, "[entire] Detected disconnected session metadata (local and remote share no common ancestor)")
   246	
   247		shallow, err := loadShallowHashes(ctx, repoPath)
   248		if err != nil {
   249			return fmt.Errorf("failed to load shallow boundaries: %w", err)
   250		}
   251	
   252		// Collect local commits oldest-first
   253		localCommits, err := collectCommitChain(repo, localHash, shallow)
   254		if err != nil {
   255			return fmt.Errorf("failed to collect local commits: %w", err)
   256		}
   257	
   258		// Filter out empty-tree commits (the orphan bug commit)
   259		var dataCommits []*object.Commit
   260		for _, c := range localCommits {
   261			tree, treeErr := c.Tree()
   262			if treeErr != nil {
   263				return fmt.Errorf("failed to read tree for commit %s: %w", c.Hash.String()[:7], treeErr)
   264			}
   265			if len(tree.Entries) > 0 {
   266				dataCommits = append(dataCommits, c)
   267			}
   268		}
   269	
   270		if len(dataCommits) == 0 {
   271			// Local only had empty orphan — just point to remote
   272			if err := advance(remoteHash); err != nil {
   273				return fmt.Errorf("failed to reset metadata ref to remote: %w", err)
   274			}
   275			fmt.Fprintln(w, "[entire] Done — local had no checkpoint data, reset to remote")
   276			return nil
   277		}
   278	
   279		fmt.Fprintf(w, "[entire] Cherry-picking %d local checkpoint(s) onto remote...\n", len(dataCommits))
   280	
   281		newTip, err := cherryPickOnto(ctx, repo, remoteHash, dataCommits, shallow)
   282		if err != nil {
   283			return fmt.Errorf("failed to cherry-pick local commits onto remote: %w", err)
   284		}
   285	
   286		if err := advance(newTip); err != nil {
   287			return fmt.Errorf("failed to update metadata ref: %w", err)
   288		}
   289	
   290		fmt.Fprintln(w, "[entire] Done — all local and remote checkpoints preserved")
   291		return nil
   292	}

   294	// isDisconnected checks if two commits have no common ancestor using git merge-base.
   295	// Returns (true, nil) if disconnected, (false, nil) if they share ancestry,
   296	// or (false, error) if git merge-base failed for another reason.
   297	//
   298	// git merge-base exit codes:
   299	//   - 0: common ancestor found (shared ancestry)
   300	//   - 1: no common ancestor (disconnected)
   301	//   - 128+: error (corrupt repo, invalid hash, etc.)
   302	func isDisconnected(ctx context.Context, repoPath, hashA, hashB string) (bool, error) {
   303		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
   304		defer cancel()
   305		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "merge-base", hashA, hashB)
   306		cmd.Dir = repoPath
   307		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
   308			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
   309			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) && exitErr.ExitCode() == 1 {
   310				return true, nil // No common ancestor — disconnected
   311			}
   312			return false, fmt.Errorf("git merge-base failed: %w", err)
   313		}
   314		return false, nil // Shared ancestry
   315	}

   317	// collectCommitChain walks from tip to root following first parent, returns oldest-first.
   318	// Commits listed in shallow are treated as roots — the walk stops at them without
   319	// traversing into their parents. go-git's repo.CommitObject().ParentHashes does not
   320	// consult .git/shallow on its own, so without this check the walk would stroll past
   321	// shallow boundaries into stale objects left in the pack (e.g., when the remote
   322	// branch has been rebuilt since the last full fetch), producing a phantom chain of
   323	// commits that no longer represent the actual checkpoint history.
   324	func collectCommitChain(repo *git.Repository, tip plumbing.Hash, shallow map[plumbing.Hash]bool) ([]*object.Commit, error) {
   325		var chain []*object.Commit
   326		current := tip
   327	
   328		reachedRoot := false
   329		for range MaxCommitTraversalDepth {
   330			commit, err := repo.CommitObject(current)
   331			if err != nil {
   332				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit %s: %w", current, err)
   333			}
   334			chain = append(chain, commit)
   335	
   336			if len(commit.ParentHashes) == 0 {
   337				reachedRoot = true
   338				break
   339			}
   340			if shallow[current] {
   341				// Shallow boundary — treat as a root.
   342				reachedRoot = true
   343				break
   344			}
   345			current = commit.ParentHashes[0]
   346		}

   360	// loadShallowHashes returns the commit hashes listed in the repository's
   361	// shallow file, or an empty map if the repository is not shallow.
   362	func loadShallowHashes(ctx context.Context, repoPath string) (map[plumbing.Hash]bool, error) {
   363		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
   364		cmd.Dir = repoPath
   365		out, err := cmd.Output()
   366		if err != nil {
   367			return nil, fmt.Errorf("git rev-parse --git-common-dir: %w", err)
   368		}
   369		gitDir := strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
   370		if !filepath.IsAbs(gitDir) {
   371			gitDir = filepath.Join(repoPath, gitDir)
   372		}
   373		// Through the common dir's root like every other read there. "shallow" is a
   374		// fixed name and gitDir came from git's own --git-common-dir, so nothing here
   375		// can traverse today; the root is what keeps that true without depending on
   376		// it, and it shares the one handle per clone.
   377		root, err := gitdir.OpenAt(gitDir)
   378		if err != nil {
   379			return nil, fmt.Errorf("open git common dir: %w", err)
   380		}
   381		data, err := osroot.ReadFileNoFollow(root, "shallow")
   382		if err != nil {
   383			if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
   384				return map[plumbing.Hash]bool{}, nil
   385			}
   386			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read shallow file: %w", err)
   387		}
   388		set := map[plumbing.Hash]bool{}
   389		for _, line := range strings.Split(string(data), "\n") {
   390			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
   391			if line == "" {
   392				continue
   393			}
   394			set[plumbing.NewHash(line)] = true
   395		}
   396		return set, nil
   397	}

   399	// cherryPickOnto applies each commit's delta onto base, building a linear chain.
   400	// For each commit, it computes the full diff from its parent (additions, modifications,
   401	// and deletions), then applies that delta onto the current tip's tree.
   402	//
   403	// Commits listed in shallow are treated as roots: their delta is computed against
   404	// an empty tree rather than against their (past-the-boundary) parent. Without this,
   405	// a shallow-boundary commit would be diffed against a stale parent tree whose
   406	// objects live in the local pack but no longer represent the actual checkpoint
   407	// history — producing nonsense changes when replayed onto the remote tip.
   408	func cherryPickOnto(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, base plumbing.Hash, commits []*object.Commit, shallow map[plumbing.Hash]bool) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   409		currentTip := base
   410	
   411		for _, commit := range commits {
   412			changes, err := treeChangesForCherryPick(ctx, repo, commit, shallow)
   413			if err != nil {
   414				return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   415			}
   416			if len(changes) == 0 {
   417				continue // Skip no-op commits
   418			}
   419	
   420			tipCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(currentTip)
   421			if err != nil {
   422				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get tip commit: %w", err)
   423			}
   424	
   425			mergedTreeHash, err := checkpoint.ApplyTreeChanges(ctx, repo, tipCommit.TreeHash, changes)
   426			if err != nil {
   427				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to apply cherry-pick changes: %w", err)
   428			}
   429			if mergedTreeHash.Equal(tipCommit.TreeHash) {
   430				continue
   431			}
   432	
   433			// Create new commit on top of current tip, preserving original message/author
   434			newHash, err := createCherryPickCommit(ctx, repo, mergedTreeHash, currentTip, commit)
   435			if err != nil {
   436				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to create cherry-pick commit: %w", err)
   437			}
   438	
   439			currentTip = newHash
   440		}
   441	
   442		return currentTip, nil
   443	}

   445	func treeChangesForCherryPick(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, commit *object.Commit, shallow map[plumbing.Hash]bool) ([]checkpoint.TreeChange, error) {
   446		commitTree, err := commit.Tree()
   447		if err != nil {
   448			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get tree for commit %s: %w", commit.Hash, err)
   449		}
   450	
   451		var parentTree *object.Tree
   452		// Shallow-boundary commits are treated as roots — see cherryPickOnto for why.
   453		if len(commit.ParentHashes) > 0 && !shallow[commit.Hash] {
   454			parentCommit, pErr := repo.CommitObject(commit.ParentHashes[0])
   455			if pErr != nil {
   456				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get parent commit %s: %w", commit.ParentHashes[0], pErr)
   457			}
   458			parentTree, err = parentCommit.Tree()
   459			if err != nil {
   460				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get parent tree for commit %s: %w", commit.ParentHashes[0], err)
   461			}
   462		}
   463	
   464		changes, err := object.DiffTreeContext(ctx, parentTree, commitTree)
   465		if err != nil {
   466			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to diff commit %s against parent: %w", commit.Hash, err)
   467		}
   468	
   469		treeChanges := make([]checkpoint.TreeChange, 0, len(changes))
   470		for _, change := range changes {
   471			treeChange, changeErr := changeToTreeChange(change)
   472			if changeErr != nil {
   473				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to convert change in commit %s: %w", commit.Hash, changeErr)
   474			}
   475			treeChanges = append(treeChanges, treeChange)
   476		}
   477		return treeChanges, nil
   478	}

   480	func changeToTreeChange(change *object.Change) (checkpoint.TreeChange, error) {
   481		action, err := change.Action()
   482		if err != nil {
   483			return checkpoint.TreeChange{}, fmt.Errorf("change action: %w", err)
   484		}
   485	
   486		switch action {
   487		case merkletrie.Insert, merkletrie.Modify:
   488			entry := change.To.TreeEntry
   489			return checkpoint.TreeChange{
   490				Path: change.To.Name,
   491				Entry: &object.TreeEntry{
   492					Name: entry.Name,
   493					Mode: entry.Mode,
   494					Hash: entry.Hash,
   495				},
   496			}, nil
   497		case merkletrie.Delete:
   498			return checkpoint.TreeChange{Path: change.From.Name}, nil
   499		default:
   500			return checkpoint.TreeChange{}, fmt.Errorf("unsupported action %s", action)
   501		}

   233	func (e *OPFRawBytesTooLargeError) Error() string {
   234		return fmt.Sprintf("OPF rewrite would buffer %d raw blob bytes across "+
   235			"all unpushed commits (limit %d, ~%d× the prose-leaf cap as a RAM ceiling). "+
   236			"Bump ENTIRE_OPF_BATCH_LIMIT (the raw ceiling scales with it) "+
   237			"or push without OPF (ENTIRE_OPF=no git push) and let a smaller "+
   238			"follow-up push run OPF",
   239			e.RawBytes, e.Limit, rawByteCapMultiplier)
   240	}
   241	
   242	// rawByteCapMultiplier ties the raw-byte RAM ceiling to the leaf-byte
   243	// inference cap. 100× means: leaf cap 2 MiB → raw ceiling 200 MiB.
   244	// Picked to comfortably exceed any realistic JSON-scaffolding ratio
   245	// (a 10 MiB JSONL with 300 KB of leaves still fits) while preventing
   246	// pathological RAM blowups (a 5 GiB pasted dump aborts before loading).
   247	const rawByteCapMultiplier = 100
   248	
   249	// RewriteUnpushedV1WithOPF re-redacts unpushed entire/checkpoints/v1
   250	// commits with OPF, builds new commits carrying Entire-OPF-Applied:
   251	// true, and CAS-updates the local ref. Idempotent: already-applied
   252	// commits are re-parented without re-running OPF.
   253	//
   254	// Caller checks redact.OPFEnabled() and skips this when OPF is off.
   255	// Returns one of {V1DivergedError, BootstrapTooLargeError,
   256	// V1RefMovedError, OPFRuntimeFailedError, OPFNoCategoriesError,
   257	// OPFBatchTooLargeError, OPFRawBytesTooLargeError} for
   258	// privacy-critical failures — the pre-push hook propagates these so
   259	// git push aborts.
   260	func RewriteUnpushedV1WithOPF(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, target string) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   261		return rewriteUnpushedV1WithOPF(ctx, repo, target, OversizedCheckpointMetadataThreshold)
   262	}
   263	
   264	func rewriteUnpushedV1WithOPF(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, target string, metadataThreshold int64) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   265		localTip, err := readV1Tip(repo, plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName))
   266		if err != nil {
   267			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("read local v1: %w", err)
   268		}
   269		if localTip.IsZero() {
   270			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil // no checkpoints yet
   271		}
   272		remoteTip, err := resolveRemoteV1Tip(ctx, repo, target)
   273		if err != nil {
   274			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("read remote v1: %w", err)
   275		}
   276	
   277		reconciledTip, handled, reconcileErr := reconcileOversizedV1ForPush(
   278			ctx, repo, localTip, remoteTip, metadataThreshold,
   279		)
   280		if reconcileErr != nil {
   281			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("reconcile oversized checkpoint metadata: %w", reconcileErr)
   282		}
   283		if handled {
   284			localTip = reconciledTip
   285		}
   286	
   287		if !remoteTip.IsZero() {
   288			mergeBase, mbErr := computeMergeBase(repo, localTip, remoteTip)
   289			if mbErr != nil {
   290				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("compute merge-base: %w", mbErr)
   291			}
   292			if mergeBase != remoteTip {
   293				return plumbing.ZeroHash, &V1DivergedError{Local: localTip, Remote: remoteTip, MergeBase: mergeBase}
   294			}
   295		}
   296	
   297		unpushed, err := listUnpushedV1Commits(repo, localTip, remoteTip)
   298		if err != nil {
   299			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("list unpushed v1 commits: %w", err)
   300		}
   301		if len(unpushed) == 0 {
   302			return localTip, nil
   303		}
   304		if remoteTip.IsZero() {
   305			if limit := resolveBootstrapLimit(); len(unpushed) > limit {
   306				return plumbing.ZeroHash, &BootstrapTooLargeError{Count: len(unpushed), Limit: limit}
   307			}
   308		}
   309	
   310		// Fail-closed defense: enabled-with-no-categories means the model
   311		// scan can't run at all. The decision resolution in prePush already
   312		// rejects this state before any prompt; this second gate covers
   313		// direct callers and sits before the breaker check so the user gets
   314		// the config-specific remediation rather than OPFRuntimeFailedError's
   315		// "verify your OPF install".
   316		if redact.OPFMisconfiguredNoCategories() {
   317			return plumbing.ZeroHash, &OPFNoCategoriesError{}
   318		}
   319	
   320		// Fail-closed defense: if OPF is already broken at the start of
   321		// this push (an earlier process step tripped the breaker), abort
   322		// before tagging any commits as OPF-applied. Without this, the
   323		// per-blob fallback inside the no-OPF cases of BatchBytesWithPrivacyFilter
   324		// could let regex-only content slip out with the trailer attached.
   325		if redact.OPFBreakerTripped() {
   326			return plumbing.ZeroHash, &OPFRuntimeFailedError{OPFCommand: redact.OPFCommand()}
   327		}
   328	
   329		// Pass 1: collect every redactable blob from every unpushed commit
   330		// that still needs OPF. Already-applied commits get re-parented
   331		// later without collecting (their tree stays as-is). We also track
   332		// each blob's source commit + tree path so we can route the redacted
   333		// bytes back during apply.
   334		type pendingCommit struct {
   335			commit *object.Commit
   336			// blobs and paths are parallel slices; len(paths)==len(blobs).
   337			// startIdx is this commit's offset into the global redacted slice.
   338			blobs    []redact.NamedBlob
   339			paths    []string
   340			startIdx int
   341		}
   342		var globalBlobs []redact.NamedBlob
   343		pendings := make([]pendingCommit, 0, len(unpushed))
   344		// Bound raw-bytes-in-memory incrementally so a pathological push
   345		// (e.g. 5 GiB of pasted dumps) aborts before exhausting the user's
   346		// shell RAM. The leaf-byte cap downstream is about inference cost;
   347		// this one is about memory ceiling and fires earlier. scaleBatchLimit
   348		// saturates at math.MaxInt so "unlimited" actually means unlimited
   349		// — without saturation, "unlimited" × 100 overflows int and the cap
   350		// trips on every push.
   351		rawCap := scaleBatchLimit(resolveBatchLimit(), rawByteCapMultiplier)
   352		var rawBytesSoFar int
   353		for _, c := range unpushed {
   354			pc := pendingCommit{commit: c}
   355			if !trailers.HasOPFApplied(c.Message) {
   356				tree, err := repo.TreeObject(c.TreeHash)
   357				if err != nil {
   358					return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("load tree for %s: %w", c.Hash.String()[:7], err)
   359				}
   360				pc.startIdx = len(globalBlobs)
   361				// Whole-tree redaction: each v1 commit tree is cumulative, so the
   362				// newest commit can still carry older shards that were regex-only
   363				// before this rewrite. Redacting the whole tree for every unapplied
   364				// commit keeps the final rewritten tip from reintroducing an
   365				// un-OPF-redacted older shard. collect and apply walk the tree the
   366				// same way so the cached keys line up.
   367				if err := collectTreeBlobs(repo, tree, "", &pc.blobs, &pc.paths); err != nil {
   368					return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("collect blobs %s: %w", c.Hash.String()[:7], err)
   369				}
   370				for _, b := range pc.blobs {
   371					rawBytesSoFar += len(b.Content)
   372				}
   373				if rawBytesSoFar > rawCap {
   374					return plumbing.ZeroHash, &OPFRawBytesTooLargeError{RawBytes: rawBytesSoFar, Limit: rawCap}
   375				}
   376				globalBlobs = append(globalBlobs, pc.blobs...)
   377			}
   378			pendings = append(pendings, pc)
   379		}
   380	
   381		// Pass 2: enforce the leaf-byte cap, then make exactly ONE OPF
   382		// shell-out for the whole push. The cap runs before the shell-out
   383		// so a too-large push fails fast with a clear remediation message.
   384		var globalRedacted [][]byte
   385		if len(globalBlobs) > 0 {
   386			leafBytes := redact.SumProseLeafBytes(globalBlobs)
   387			if limit := resolveBatchLimit(); leafBytes > limit {
   388				return plumbing.ZeroHash, &OPFBatchTooLargeError{LeafBytes: leafBytes, Limit: limit}
   389			}
   390			globalRedacted, err = redact.BatchBytesWithPrivacyFilter(ctx, globalBlobs)
   391			if err != nil {
   392				// Converge with the up-front gate: the misconfiguration
   393				// sentinel must surface config remediation, not "verify
   394				// your OPF install".
   395				if errors.Is(err, redact.ErrOPFNoEnabledCategories) {
   396					return plumbing.ZeroHash, &OPFNoCategoriesError{}
   397				}
   398				return plumbing.ZeroHash, &OPFRuntimeFailedError{OPFCommand: redact.OPFCommand(), Cause: err}
   399			}
   400		}
   401	
   402		// Pass 3: rebuild each commit. For OPF-applied commits, this is
   403		// just a re-parent (no tree changes). For unapplied commits, the
   404		// per-commit redaction map routes cached bytes by tree path.
   405		parent := remoteTip
   406		for _, pc := range pendings {
   407			var redactedByPath map[string][]byte
   408			if len(pc.blobs) > 0 {
   409				redactedByPath = make(map[string][]byte, len(pc.blobs))
   410				for i, path := range pc.paths {
   411					redactedByPath[path] = globalRedacted[pc.startIdx+i]
   412				}
   413			}
   414			newHash, err := rebuildCheckpointCommit(ctx, repo, pc.commit, parent, redactedByPath)
   415			if err != nil {
   416				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("rebuild commit %s: %w", pc.commit.Hash.String()[:7], err)
   417			}
   418			parent = newHash
   419		}
   420	
   421		if err := atomicSetV1Ref(ctx, repo, localTip, parent); err != nil {
   422			return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   423		}
   424		return parent, nil
   425	}

   427	func readV1Tip(repo *git.Repository, refName plumbing.ReferenceName) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   428		ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   429		if err != nil {
   430			if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   431				return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil
   432			}
   433			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("resolve ref %s: %w", refName, err)
   434		}
   435		return ref.Hash(), nil
   436	}

   438	// opfRewriteFetchTmpRef is the temp ref used to stage the URL-fetched
   439	// remote v1 tip during OPF rewrite. Cleaned up at the end of each
   440	// resolveRemoteV1Tip call so the tracking is invisible to the user.
   441	const opfRewriteFetchTmpRef = FetchTmpRefPrefix + "opf-rewrite-v1"
   442	
   443	// resolveRemoteV1Tip returns the hash of the remote's
   444	// entire/checkpoints/v1 tip.
   445	//
   446	// Fetches the v1 ref from target into a temporary local ref so the
   447	// rewrite compares against the current remote tip rather than a stale
   448	// remote-tracking ref. target may be either a remote name (e.g. "origin")
   449	// or a URL (checkpoint_remote configured). Fetching is especially important
   450	// for URL-based remotes, which have no tracking refs locally; otherwise every
   451	// push would re-redact the entire history as a "bootstrap."
   452	//
   453	// Returns ZeroHash with no error when the remote has no v1 yet (genuine
   454	// bootstrap case). Fetch failures fall back to ZeroHash + a warning
   455	// log; the rewrite then treats the push as bootstrap rather than
   456	// blocking the user on a transient network issue.
   457	func resolveRemoteV1Tip(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, target string) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   458		srcRef := "refs/heads/" + paths.MetadataBranchName
   459		worktreeRoot := ""
   460		if wt, wtErr := repo.Worktree(); wtErr == nil {
   461			worktreeRoot = wt.Filesystem().Root()
   462		}
   463		if err := fetchURLIntoTmpRef(ctx, worktreeRoot, target, srcRef, opfRewriteFetchTmpRef, "v1 for OPF rewrite", true, checkpointRemoteFetchTimeout); err != nil {
   464			if !remote.IsURL(target) {
   465				logging.Warn(ctx, "OPF rewrite: failed to fetch remote v1; using local remote-tracking ref",
   466					slog.String("remote", target),
   467					slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   468				)
   469				return readV1Tip(repo, plumbing.NewRemoteReferenceName(target, paths.MetadataBranchName))
   470			}
   471			logging.Warn(ctx, "OPF rewrite: failed to fetch remote v1 from URL; treating push as bootstrap",
   472				slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   473			)
   474			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil
   475		}
   476		defer func() {
   477			if err := repo.Storer.RemoveReference(plumbing.ReferenceName(opfRewriteFetchTmpRef)); err != nil {
   478				logging.Debug(ctx, "OPF rewrite: failed to clean up temp ref",
   479					slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   480				)
   481			}
   482		}()
   483		ref, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.ReferenceName(opfRewriteFetchTmpRef), true)
   484		if err != nil {
   485			if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   486				return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil
   487			}

   493	// computeMergeBase returns the merge-base commit hash. Multi-base
   494	// (criss-cross) and unrelated-histories both return ZeroHash —
   495	// caller treats those as diverged.
   496	func computeMergeBase(repo *git.Repository, local, remote plumbing.Hash) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   497		lc, err := repo.CommitObject(local)
   498		if err != nil {
   499			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("load local commit: %w", err)
   500		}
   501		rc, err := repo.CommitObject(remote)
   502		if err != nil {
   503			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("load remote commit: %w", err)
   504		}
   505		bases, err := lc.MergeBase(rc)
   506		if err != nil {
   507			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("merge-base: %w", err)
   508		}
   509		if len(bases) != 1 {
   510			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil
   511		}
   512		return bases[0].Hash, nil
   513	}
   514	
   515	// listUnpushedV1Commits returns commits reachable from localTip but not
   516	// remoteTip, in graph order (oldest-first). Graph order matters more
   517	// than timestamp order — commits made in rapid succession can share
   518	// Author.When; the parent chain is the unambiguous truth.
   519	//
   520	// Optimization: the caller (RewriteUnpushedV1WithOPF) has already
   521	// validated that remoteTip is the unique merge-base of local and
   522	// remote, which means v1 is linear and remoteTip is an ancestor of
   523	// localTip. So walking back from localTip, the FIRST commit we hit
   524	// whose hash equals remoteTip is the boundary — no need to pre-build
   525	// a full remote-reachability set. This drops the cost from
   526	// O(local + remote history) to O(unpushed) per call.
   527	func listUnpushedV1Commits(repo *git.Repository, localTip, remoteTip plumbing.Hash) ([]*object.Commit, error) {
   528		iter, err := repo.Log(&git.LogOptions{From: localTip})
   529		if err != nil {
   530			return nil, fmt.Errorf("log local tip: %w", err)
   531		}
   532		defer iter.Close()
   533	
   534		var unpushed []*object.Commit
   535		if walkErr := iter.ForEach(func(c *object.Commit) error {
   536			if !remoteTip.IsZero() && c.Hash.Equal(remoteTip) {
   537				return errStop
   538			}
   539			unpushed = append(unpushed, c)
   540			return nil

   137	// against the first checkpoint read candidate whose remote-tracking ref
   138	// exists (pure read across both tiers).

   143	// invocation-scoped remote-read cache, re-shelling out for answers the caller
   144	// already had.

   154					slog.String("error", err.Error()))

   156			}

   171			}

   174			}

   399	// cherryPickOnto applies each commit's delta onto base, building a linear chain.
   400	// For each commit, it computes the full diff from its parent (additions, modifications,
   401	// and deletions), then applies that delta onto the current tip's tree.
   402	//
   403	// Commits listed in shallow are treated as roots: their delta is computed against
   404	// an empty tree rather than against their (past-the-boundary) parent. Without this,
   405	// a shallow-boundary commit would be diffed against a stale parent tree whose
   406	// objects live in the local pack but no longer represent the actual checkpoint
   407	// history — producing nonsense changes when replayed onto the remote tip.
   408	func cherryPickOnto(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, base plumbing.Hash, commits []*object.Commit, shallow map[plumbing.Hash]bool) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   409		currentTip := base
   410	
   411		for _, commit := range commits {
   412			changes, err := treeChangesForCherryPick(ctx, repo, commit, shallow)
   413			if err != nil {
   414				return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   415			}
   416			if len(changes) == 0 {
   417				continue // Skip no-op commits
   418			}
   419	
   420			tipCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(currentTip)
   421			if err != nil {
   422				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get tip commit: %w", err)
   423			}
   424	
   425			mergedTreeHash, err := checkpoint.ApplyTreeChanges(ctx, repo, tipCommit.TreeHash, changes)
   426			if err != nil {
   427				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to apply cherry-pick changes: %w", err)
   428			}
   429			if mergedTreeHash.Equal(tipCommit.TreeHash) {
   430				continue
   431			}
   432	
   433			// Create new commit on top of current tip, preserving original message/author
   434			newHash, err := createCherryPickCommit(ctx, repo, mergedTreeHash, currentTip, commit)
   435			if err != nil {
   436				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to create cherry-pick commit: %w", err)
   437			}
   438	
   439			currentTip = newHash
   440		}
   441	
   442		return currentTip, nil
   443	}

   445	func treeChangesForCherryPick(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, commit *object.Commit, shallow map[plumbing.Hash]bool) ([]checkpoint.TreeChange, error) {
   446		commitTree, err := commit.Tree()
   447		if err != nil {
   448			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get tree for commit %s: %w", commit.Hash, err)
   449		}
   450	
   451		var parentTree *object.Tree
   452		// Shallow-boundary commits are treated as roots — see cherryPickOnto for why.
   453		if len(commit.ParentHashes) > 0 && !shallow[commit.Hash] {
   454			parentCommit, pErr := repo.CommitObject(commit.ParentHashes[0])
   455			if pErr != nil {
   456				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get parent commit %s: %w", commit.ParentHashes[0], pErr)
   457			}
   458			parentTree, err = parentCommit.Tree()
   459			if err != nil {
   460				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get parent tree for commit %s: %w", commit.ParentHashes[0], err)
   461			}
   462		}
   463	
   464		changes, err := object.DiffTreeContext(ctx, parentTree, commitTree)
   465		if err != nil {
   466			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to diff commit %s against parent: %w", commit.Hash, err)
   467		}
   468	
   469		treeChanges := make([]checkpoint.TreeChange, 0, len(changes))
   470		for _, change := range changes {
   471			treeChange, changeErr := changeToTreeChange(change)
   472			if changeErr != nil {
   473				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to convert change in commit %s: %w", commit.Hash, changeErr)
   474			}
   475			treeChanges = append(treeChanges, treeChange)
   476		}
   477		return treeChanges, nil
   478	}

   163	// doPushRef pushes the given ref to the target with fetch+rebase recovery.
   164	// The target can be a remote name or a URL.
   165	//
   166	// The error return is fail-soft by design and is nil on every push failure: a
   167	// checkpoint that cannot be synced must never break the user's own `git push`.
   168	// That makes err useless as a "did it land" signal, so delivery is reported
   169	// separately — delivered is true only where finishPush runs, meaning the ref is
   170	// on the target (freshly pushed or already up-to-date). Callers that act on
   171	// delivery, such as latching the captured checkpoint sync remote, must read
   172	// delivered and not err.
   173	func doPushRef(ctx context.Context, target string, ref plumbing.ReferenceName) (delivered bool, err error) {

   177	func doPushRefWithMetadataThreshold(ctx context.Context, target string, ref plumbing.ReferenceName, metadataThreshold int64) (delivered bool, err error) {
   178		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, checkpointPushBudget)
   179		defer cancel()
   180	
   181		displayTarget := displayPushTarget(target)
   182		refLabel := refDisplayName(ref)
   183	
   184		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Pushing %s to %s...", refLabel, displayTarget)
   185		stop := startProgressDots(os.Stderr)
   186	
   187		// Try pushing first
   188		result, err := tryPushRefCommon(ctx, target, ref)
   189		if err == nil {
   190			finishPush(ctx, stop, result, target)
   191			return true, nil
   192		}
   193		stop("")
   194	
   195		// Protected refs cannot be fixed by syncing and retrying.
   196		var protectedErr *protectedRefError
   197		if errors.As(err, &protectedErr) {
   198			printProtectedRefBlock(os.Stderr, refLabel, target)
   199			return false, nil
   200		}
   201	
   202		// Non-interactive SSH (pre-push BatchMode): auth failures cannot be fixed by
   203		// fetch+rebase, and retrying would just reprint the same opaque error.
   204		// Surface an actionable ssh-agent hint and skip recovery (issue #1523).
   205		if nonInteractiveSSHAuthFailure(ctx, err) {
   206			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: couldn't push %s: %v\n", refLabel, err)
   207			printNonInteractiveSSHAuthHint()
   208			printCheckpointRemoteHint(target)
   209			return false, nil
   210		}
   211	
   212		// Push failed - likely non-fast-forward. Try to fetch and rebase.
   213		// Spanned (with the network fetch as a child) so the trace distinguishes
   214		// "the raw push is slow" from "we keep hitting contention and re-syncing".
   215		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Syncing %s with remote...", refLabel)
   216		stop = startProgressDots(os.Stderr)
   217	
   218		frCtx, fetchRebaseSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "fetch_and_rebase")
   219		syncErr := fetchAndRebaseRefWithMetadataThreshold(frCtx, target, ref, metadataThreshold)
   220		fetchRebaseSpan.RecordError(syncErr)
   221		fetchRebaseSpan.End()
   222		if syncErr != nil {
   223			stop("")
   224			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: couldn't sync %s: %v\n", refLabel, syncErr)
   225			if nonInteractiveSSHAuthFailure(ctx, syncErr) {
   226				printNonInteractiveSSHAuthHint()
   227			}
   228			printCheckpointRemoteHint(target)
   229			return false, nil // Don't fail the main push
   230		}
   231		stop(" done")
   232	
   233		// Try pushing again after rebase
   234		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Pushing %s to %s...", refLabel, displayTarget)
   235		stop = startProgressDots(os.Stderr)
   236	
   237		result, retryErr := tryPushRefCommon(ctx, target, ref)
   238		if retryErr != nil {
   239			stop("")
   240			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: failed to push %s after sync: %v\n", refLabel, retryErr)
   241			if nonInteractiveSSHAuthFailure(ctx, retryErr) {
   242				printNonInteractiveSSHAuthHint()
   243			}
   244			printCheckpointRemoteHint(target)
   245			return false, nil
   246		}
   247		finishPush(ctx, stop, result, target)
   248		return true, nil
   249	}

   476	// of the remote tip. Since checkpoint shards use unique paths, rebases always

   482	
   483	func fetchAndRebaseRefWithMetadataThreshold(ctx context.Context, target string, ref plumbing.ReferenceName, metadataThreshold int64) error {
   484		// No timeout: runs under doPushRef's shared budget.
   485		fetchTarget, err := remote.ResolveFetchTarget(ctx, target)
   486		if err != nil {
   487			return fmt.Errorf("resolve fetch target: %w", err)
   488		}
   489	
   490		// Determine fetch refspec. When the resolved fetch target is a URL or the
   491		// ref isn't a branch, fetch into a temp ref (no remote-tracking shadow);
   492		// otherwise use the standard refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch> destination.
   493		var fetchedRefName plumbing.ReferenceName
   494		var refSpec string
   495		usedTempRef := remote.IsURL(fetchTarget) || !ref.IsBranch()
   496		if usedTempRef {
   497			tmpRef := "refs/entire-fetch-tmp/" + strings.TrimPrefix(ref.String(), "refs/")
   498			refSpec = fmt.Sprintf("+%s:%s", ref.String(), tmpRef)
   499			fetchedRefName = plumbing.ReferenceName(tmpRef)
   500		} else {
   501			refSpec = fmt.Sprintf("+%s:refs/remotes/%s/%s", ref.String(), target, ref.Short())
   502			fetchedRefName = plumbing.NewRemoteReferenceName(target, ref.Short())
   503		}
   504	
   505		// Use git CLI for fetch (go-git's fetch can be tricky with auth).
   506		// Do NOT --unshallow here: on a shallow repo with deep history (e.g. a
   507		// shared monorepo), --unshallow downloads the whole repository because
   508		// git treats shallow as a global property of the clone, not per-ref.
   509		// The downstream reconcile/rebase paths walk only commits visible past
   510		// .git/shallow (collectCommitChain / collectCommitsSince), so the
   511		// missing pre-shallow history isn't needed to produce a correct rebase.
   512		// Span the fetch separately so a slow sync can be attributed to the network
   513		// fetch versus the local reconcile/rebase that follows it.
   514		_, fetchSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "git_fetch")
   515		fetchOutput, fetchErr := remote.Fetch(ctx, remote.FetchOptions{
   516			Remote:   fetchTarget,
   517			RefSpecs: []string{refSpec},
   518			NoTags:   true,
   519		})
   520		fetchSpan.RecordError(fetchErr)
   521		fetchSpan.End()
   522		if fetchErr != nil {
   523			return fmt.Errorf("fetch failed: %s", fetchOutput)
   524		}
   525	
   526		repo, err := OpenRepository(ctx)
   527		if err != nil {
   528			return fmt.Errorf("failed to open git repository: %w", err)
   529		}
   530		defer repo.Close()
   531	
   532		// Reconcile disconnected metadata branches before rebasing.
   533		// The fetch above updated the remote-tracking ref, so reconciliation
   534		// can compare fresh local vs remote. If disconnected (empty-orphan bug),
   535		// this cherry-picks local commits onto remote tip, updating the local ref.
   536		// If reconciliation fails, abort — proceeding to rebase on disconnected
   537		// refs would silently combine unrelated histories.
   538		if reconcileErr := ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataRef(ctx, repo, ref, fetchedRefName, os.Stderr); reconcileErr != nil {
   539			return fmt.Errorf("metadata reconciliation failed: %w", reconcileErr)
   540		}
   541	
   542		// Get local ref (re-read after potential reconciliation update)
   543		localRef, err := repo.Reference(ref, true)
   544		if err != nil {
   545			return fmt.Errorf("failed to get local ref: %w", err)
   546		}
   547	
   548		// Get fetched ref (remote-tracking or temp ref, updated by the fetch above)
   549		remoteRef, err := repo.Reference(fetchedRefName, true)
   550		if err != nil {
   551			return fmt.Errorf("failed to get remote ref: %w", err)
   552		}
   553	
   554		advance := func(hash plumbing.Hash) error {
   555			if err := setRefHash(repo, ref, hash); err != nil {
   556				return err
   557			}
   558			if usedTempRef {
   559				_ = repo.Storer.RemoveReference(fetchedRefName) //nolint:errcheck // cleanup is best-effort
   560			}
   561			return nil
   562		}
   563	
   564		// If local is already at or behind remote, fast-forward
   565		if localRef.Hash().Equal(remoteRef.Hash()) {
   566			return advance(remoteRef.Hash())
   567		}
   568		if ref == plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName) {
   569			_, handled, reconcileErr := reconcileOversizedV1ForPush(
   570				ctx, repo, localRef.Hash(), remoteRef.Hash(), metadataThreshold,
   571			)
   572			if reconcileErr != nil {
   573				return fmt.Errorf("reconcile oversized checkpoint metadata: %w", reconcileErr)
   574			}
   575			if handled {
   576				if usedTempRef {
   577					_ = repo.Storer.RemoveReference(fetchedRefName) //nolint:errcheck // cleanup is best-effort
   578				}
   579				return nil
   580			}
   581		}
   582	
   583		// Find merge base
   584		repoPath, err := getRepoPath(repo)
   585		if err != nil {
   586			return fmt.Errorf("failed to get repo path: %w", err)
   587		}
   588		mergeBase, err := getMergeBase(ctx, repoPath, localRef.Hash().String(), remoteRef.Hash().String())
   589		if err != nil {
   590			return fmt.Errorf("failed to find merge base: %w", err)
   591		}
   592	
   593		// If local is ancestor of remote (merge base == local), fast-forward to remote
   594		if mergeBase.Equal(localRef.Hash()) {
   595			if err := advance(remoteRef.Hash()); err != nil {
   596				return fmt.Errorf("failed to fast-forward ref: %w", err)
   597			}
   598			return nil
   599		}
   600	
   601		// Collect commits reachable from local but not from remote and cherry-pick
   602		// them onto the remote tip. This preserves local-only commits even when the
   603		// local metadata branch already contains old merge commits, while avoiding
   604		// replaying shared ancestors older than the true merge-base.
   605		localCommits, err := collectCommitsSince(ctx, repo, repoPath, localRef.Hash(), remoteRef.Hash())
   606		if err != nil {
   607			return fmt.Errorf("failed to collect local commits: %w", err)
   608		}
   609	
   610		if len(localCommits) == 0 {
   611			// No local-only commits — just point to remote
   612			return advance(remoteRef.Hash())
   613		}
   614	
   615		shallow, err := loadShallowHashes(ctx, repoPath)
   616		if err != nil {
   617			return fmt.Errorf("failed to load shallow boundaries: %w", err)
   618		}
   619	
   620		newTip, err := cherryPickOnto(ctx, repo, remoteRef.Hash(), localCommits, shallow)
   621		if err != nil {
   622			return fmt.Errorf("failed to rebase local commits onto remote: %w", err)
   623		}
   624	
   625		return advance(newTip)
   626	}

   628	// getMergeBase returns the merge base hash of two commits, or an error if they
   629	// have no common ancestor.
   630	func getMergeBase(ctx context.Context, repoPath, hashA, hashB string) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   631		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
   632		defer cancel()
   633	
   634		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "merge-base", hashA, hashB)
   635		cmd.Dir = repoPath
   636		output, err := cmd.Output()
   637		if err != nil {
   638			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
   639			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) && exitErr.ExitCode() == 1 {
   640				return plumbing.ZeroHash, errNoMergeBase
   641			}
   642			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("git merge-base failed: %w", err)
   643		}
   644	
   645		mergeBase := strings.TrimSpace(string(output))
   646		if mergeBase == "" {

   247	// opfGateForCheckpointRefs resolves the OPF decision and, when it says run,
   248	// rewrites the queued checkpoint refs. A nil error means the flush may proceed;
   249	// a non-nil one means it must be withheld, leaving the refs queued rather than
   250	// shipping 8-layer content the user did not opt out of. OPF being disabled is a
   251	// nil error, so every flush can call this unconditionally.
   252	//
   253	// Every path that flushes the queue must pass through here, because skipping it
   254	// is not the same as an OPFSkip: a skip is a decision the user made for this
   255	// push and it ships untagged content deliberately, while a missing gate ships
   256	// exactly the same bytes having never asked.
   257	//
   258	// Reporting belongs to the caller: the pre-push hook warns and carries on,
   259	// because a checkpoint failure must never block the user's own git push, while
   260	// an explicitly requested push surfaces the error instead.
   261	//
   262	// Precondition, and the one way to make this gate a silent no-op: OPFEnabled
   263	// reads process-global config that only EnsureRedactionConfigured sets, so a
   264	// caller that reaches here without it having run reads "OPF off" and flushes
   265	// everything unscanned. Every caller must ensure it — the hook path via
   266	// withHookSession (hooks_git_cmd.go), the migration push via pushMigratedRefs
   267	// (doctor_migrate.go).
   268	//
   269	// This gate does not call it itself: on the hook path its scanner-config error
   270	// is deliberately logged and survived rather than propagated, so raising it
   271	// here would withhold pushes on a condition that path documents as
   272	// non-fatal.
   273	func opfGateForCheckpointRefs(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository) error {
   274		if !redact.OPFEnabled() {
   275			return nil
   276		}
   277		decision, err := opfPrePushDecision(ctx)
   278		if err != nil {
   279			return err
   280		}
   281		switch decision {
   282		case OPFAbort:
   283			return ErrOPFAbortedByUser
   284		case OPFSkip:
   285			// Explicit opt-out for this push: flush the 8-layer content as-is,
   286			// untagged — same as the v1 path.
   287			logging.Info(ctx, "OPF skipped for this push (user choice or settings)")
   288		case OPFRun:
   289			_, opfSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "opf_pre_push_rewrite_refs")
   290			defer opfSpan.End()
   291			if rewriteErr := RewriteQueuedCheckpointRefsWithOPF(ctx, repo); rewriteErr != nil {
   292				opfSpan.RecordError(rewriteErr)
   293				return rewriteErr
   294			}
   295		}
   296		return nil
   297	}

   301	// is never the first they hear of it.
   302	//
   303	// Names no cause, for the reason PushQueuedCheckpointRefs does not either: the
   304	// gate withholds on an unresolvable decision or a failed scan, but also on a

   317	// deferCheckpointPushOnEmptyRemote reports whether publication of the git-branch
   318	// v1 metadata should be held back because the push remote may be brand new.
   319	//
   320	// Hosting providers such as GitHub make the first branch pushed to an empty
   321	// repository its default, so the pre-push hook must not publish
   322	// entire/checkpoints/v1 ahead of the user's own first branch. The check is
   323	// purely local: if a remote-tracking ref for this remote already exists
   324	// (refs/remotes/<remote>/*), the remote has been fetched from or pushed to
   325	// before and therefore already has at least one branch, so publishing cannot
   326	// make our metadata the default. Otherwise defer — git records a
   327	// remote-tracking ref after the first successful push, so the deferred metadata
   328	// publishes on the next push.
   329	//
   330	// It deliberately performs no ls-remote/fetch. A network round trip on the
   331	// pre-push path can trigger an SSH security-key touch prompt (and doing so per
   332	// push URL would multiply those prompts), which is a poor pre-push UX. This is
   333	// also why it uses only the remote git handed the hook rather than resolving
   334	// every configured push URL.
   335	//
   336	// A separate checkpoint remote is exempt: it is a dedicated metadata store, not
   337	// the repository the user pushes to.
   338	func deferCheckpointPushOnEmptyRemote(ctx context.Context, ps pushSettings) bool {
   339		if ps.hasCheckpointURL() {
   340			return false
   341		}
   342	
   343		// The hazard only arises for a configured remote (the `git remote add
   344		// origin …` then first-push flow). Pushing straight to a bare URL hands that
   345		// URL to the hook as the remote arg, and git never records a
   346		// refs/remotes/<url>/* tracking ref for it — so a tracking-ref check would
   347		// defer the metadata forever. Publish for a non-configured (URL) target
   348		// rather than strand it; the first-branch scenario always uses a named
   349		// remote.
   350		if !isConfiguredRemote(ctx, ps.remote) {
   351			return false
   352		}
   353	
   354		// Known limitation, accepted for the no-network design: a tracking ref left
   355		// over from before a remote was deleted and recreated empty under the same
   356		// URL reads as "established", so v1 would publish to the now-empty remote.
   357		// Detecting that requires asking the remote — the network round trip we
   358		// deliberately avoid here. The scenario is rare and its default branch is
   359		// recoverable by resetting it on the forge.
   360		return !remoteHasTrackingRefs(ctx, ps.remote)
   361	}

   363	// isConfiguredRemote reports whether name is a configured git remote, as
   364	// opposed to a bare URL that git passes through verbatim when a push targets a
   365	// URL directly. Local and best-effort (reads config, no network); any error is
   366	// treated as "not a configured remote".
   367	func isConfiguredRemote(ctx context.Context, name string) bool {
   368		if name == "" {
   369			return false
   370		}
   371		return cachedIsConfiguredRemote(ctx, name, func() (bool, error) {
   372			cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "remote", "get-url", name)
   373			if worktreeRoot, ok := settings.WorktreeRoot(ctx); ok {
   374				cmd.Dir = worktreeRoot
   375			}
   376			err := cmd.Run()
   377			if err == nil {
   378				return true, nil
   379			}
   380			// git ran and said no: a real answer worth caching. git failing to run at
   381			// all says nothing about the remote, and memoizing that false would
   382			// fail-close checkpoint_push_remote for the rest of the process.
   383			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
   384			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
   385				return false, nil
   386			}
   387			return false, fmt.Errorf("probe remote %q: %w", name, err)
   388		})
   389	}

   391	// remoteHasTrackingRefs reports whether any refs/remotes/<remote>/* ref exists
   392	// locally. Its presence means the remote has been fetched from or pushed to
   393	// before and so already has at least one branch. Local-only and best-effort:
   394	// any error is treated as "no tracking refs" so the caller fails safe (defers).
   395	func remoteHasTrackingRefs(ctx context.Context, remote string) bool {
   396		if remote == "" {
   397			return false
   398		}
   399		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "for-each-ref", "--count=1", "refs/remotes/"+remote+"/")
   400		out, err := cmd.Output()
   401		if err != nil {
   402			return false
   403		}
   404		return strings.TrimSpace(string(out)) != ""
   405	}

   407	// prePushCheckpointRefs drains the per-checkpoint push queue and batch-pushes the
   408	// recorded refs fast-forward-only (git-refs primary; never a force push — a
   409	// diverged ref is recovered via fetch+replay). Transient push failures are logged and
   410	// swallowed — like the v1 path, they must not block the user's git push — and the
   411	// refs stay queued for the next pre-push. When OPF is enabled the queued refs
   412	// are re-redacted with it first (RewriteQueuedCheckpointRefsWithOPF).
   413	//
   414	// It honors the checkpoint policy exactly like the v1 path: the policy gates on
   415	// checkpoint *format* compatibility (diverged from the remote, or an unsupported
   416	// local format), which is independent of the storage backend, so a blocked
   417	// policy skips the ref push (leaving refs queued) rather than pushing.
   418	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) prePushCheckpointRefs(ctx context.Context, ps pushSettings, pendingCapture string) error {
   419		repo, err := OpenRepository(ctx)
   420		if err != nil {
   421			logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs pre-push: open repo failed; skipping checkpoint push",
   422				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   423			return nil
   424		}
   425		defer repo.Close()
   426	
   427		// Refresh the checkpoint policy from the remote, then skip the ref push
   428		// (leaving refs queued) if the policy is diverged or the local format is
   429		// unsupported — same gate the v1 path uses.
   430		syncCheckpointPolicyForPrePush(ctx, repo, ps)
   431		if !checkpointPolicyAllowsGitHook(ctx, repo) {
   432			return nil
   433		}
   434	
   435		// OPF backend divergence: both paths fail closed, but this one does it
   436		// without blocking the user. The v1 path aborts the user's git push; here a
   437		// checkpoint-ref failure must never do that (see this function's doc), so
   438		// failing closed means withholding the flush — nothing un-OPF'd ships, the
   439		// refs stay queued, and the user's push proceeds.
   440		if opfErr := opfGateForCheckpointRefs(ctx, repo); opfErr != nil {
   441			warnOPFCheckpointRefsWithheld(ctx, opfErr)
   442			return nil
   443		}
   444	
   445		if flushed, err := flushCheckpointRefsQueue(ctx, repo, ps); err == nil {
   446			// Delivered, and only if something actually was: an empty queue pushed
   447			// nothing, so it must not move the election or announce that it had.
   448			if pendingCapture != "" && flushed > 0 {
   449				commitCapturedSyncRemote(ctx, pendingCapture)
   450			}
   451		} else {
   452			// Fail-soft: a checkpoint-ref push failure must never block the user's
   453			// git push. The refs stay queued for the next pre-push.
   454			logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs pre-push: checkpoint ref push failed; refs left queued",
   455				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   456		}
   457	
   458		cleanupPushedShadowBranches(ctx)
   459		return nil
   460	}

   462	// PushQueuedCheckpointRefs pushes any queued checkpoint refs to the configured
   463	// checkpoint remote, surfacing errors (unlike the fail-soft pre-push path); the
   464	// caller owns the repo. It returns the number of refs pushed and whether
   465	// pushing is disabled in settings — a distinct signal from pushed==0 with
   466	// pushing enabled (an empty queue), so callers can report the two accurately.
   467	// Like the pre-push paths, a checkpoint policy that blocks pushing — or, when
   468	// OPF is enabled, an OPF rewrite that cannot run — errors with the refs left
   469	// queued. Currently used by the checkpoint migration command's opt-in
   470	// "push now".
   471	func PushQueuedCheckpointRefs(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, remote string) (pushed int, pushDisabled bool, err error) {
   472		ps := resolvePushSettings(ctx, remote)
   473		if ps.pushDisabled {
   474			return 0, true, nil
   475		}
   476		syncCheckpointPolicyForPrePush(ctx, repo, ps)
   477		if !checkpointPolicyAllowsGitHook(ctx, repo) {
   478			return 0, false, errors.New("checkpoint policy does not allow pushing checkpoint refs; refs stay queued")
   479		}
   480		if opfErr := opfGateForCheckpointRefs(ctx, repo); opfErr != nil {
   481			// Names no cause, matching flushCheckpointRefsQueue's retry message
   482			// below: the gate fails on an unresolvable decision or a failed scan,
   483			// but also on a ref update that lost a race after a scan that ran
   484			// fine, so "OPF did not run" would sometimes send the user after the
   485			// wrong problem. The wrapped error says which it was.
   486			return 0, false, fmt.Errorf("checkpoint refs stay queued: %w", opfErr)
   487		}
   488		pushed, err = flushCheckpointRefsQueue(ctx, repo, ps)
   489		// Clean up even on a partial/failed flush: a diverged batch can push some
   490		// refs and still return an error, and the shadow branches for the refs that
   491		// *did* land must still be cleaned up — parity with the pre-push path, which
   492		// always runs cleanup after flush regardless of its error.
   493		cleanupPushedShadowBranches(ctx)

   495	}

   497	// flushCheckpointRefsQueue drains the push-discovery queue and batch-pushes the

   499	// removing from the queue only the refs that land. It returns the number pushed.

   502	// never block the user's push) and the migration command's opt-in push (which
   503	// surfaces it). Stale entries — refs no longer present locally — are pruned so
   504	// they don't block the queue forever.
   505	func flushCheckpointRefsQueue(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, ps pushSettings) (int, error) {

   507		if err != nil {

   509		}

   511		if err != nil {

   247	// opfGateForCheckpointRefs resolves the OPF decision and, when it says run,
   248	// rewrites the queued checkpoint refs. A nil error means the flush may proceed;
   249	// a non-nil one means it must be withheld, leaving the refs queued rather than
   250	// shipping 8-layer content the user did not opt out of. OPF being disabled is a
   251	// nil error, so every flush can call this unconditionally.
   252	//
   253	// Every path that flushes the queue must pass through here, because skipping it
   254	// is not the same as an OPFSkip: a skip is a decision the user made for this
   255	// push and it ships untagged content deliberately, while a missing gate ships
   256	// exactly the same bytes having never asked.
   257	//
   258	// Reporting belongs to the caller: the pre-push hook warns and carries on,
   259	// because a checkpoint failure must never block the user's own git push, while
   260	// an explicitly requested push surfaces the error instead.
   261	//
   262	// Precondition, and the one way to make this gate a silent no-op: OPFEnabled
   263	// reads process-global config that only EnsureRedactionConfigured sets, so a
   264	// caller that reaches here without it having run reads "OPF off" and flushes
   265	// everything unscanned. Every caller must ensure it — the hook path via
   266	// withHookSession (hooks_git_cmd.go), the migration push via pushMigratedRefs
   267	// (doctor_migrate.go).
   268	//
   269	// This gate does not call it itself: on the hook path its scanner-config error
   270	// is deliberately logged and survived rather than propagated, so raising it
   271	// here would withhold pushes on a condition that path documents as
   272	// non-fatal.
   273	func opfGateForCheckpointRefs(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository) error {
   274		if !redact.OPFEnabled() {
   275			return nil
   276		}
   277		decision, err := opfPrePushDecision(ctx)
   278		if err != nil {
   279			return err
   280		}
   281		switch decision {
   282		case OPFAbort:
   283			return ErrOPFAbortedByUser
   284		case OPFSkip:
   285			// Explicit opt-out for this push: flush the 8-layer content as-is,
   286			// untagged — same as the v1 path.
   287			logging.Info(ctx, "OPF skipped for this push (user choice or settings)")
   288		case OPFRun:
   289			_, opfSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "opf_pre_push_rewrite_refs")
   290			defer opfSpan.End()
   291			if rewriteErr := RewriteQueuedCheckpointRefsWithOPF(ctx, repo); rewriteErr != nil {
   292				opfSpan.RecordError(rewriteErr)
   293				return rewriteErr
   294			}
   295		}
   296		return nil
   297	}

   317	// deferCheckpointPushOnEmptyRemote reports whether publication of the git-branch
   318	// v1 metadata should be held back because the push remote may be brand new.
   319	//
   320	// Hosting providers such as GitHub make the first branch pushed to an empty
   321	// repository its default, so the pre-push hook must not publish
   322	// entire/checkpoints/v1 ahead of the user's own first branch. The check is
   323	// purely local: if a remote-tracking ref for this remote already exists
   324	// (refs/remotes/<remote>/*), the remote has been fetched from or pushed to
   325	// before and therefore already has at least one branch, so publishing cannot
   326	// make our metadata the default. Otherwise defer — git records a
   327	// remote-tracking ref after the first successful push, so the deferred metadata
   328	// publishes on the next push.
   329	//
   330	// It deliberately performs no ls-remote/fetch. A network round trip on the
   331	// pre-push path can trigger an SSH security-key touch prompt (and doing so per
   332	// push URL would multiply those prompts), which is a poor pre-push UX. This is
   333	// also why it uses only the remote git handed the hook rather than resolving
   334	// every configured push URL.
   335	//
   336	// A separate checkpoint remote is exempt: it is a dedicated metadata store, not
   337	// the repository the user pushes to.
   338	func deferCheckpointPushOnEmptyRemote(ctx context.Context, ps pushSettings) bool {
   339		if ps.hasCheckpointURL() {
   340			return false
   341		}
   342	
   343		// The hazard only arises for a configured remote (the `git remote add
   344		// origin …` then first-push flow). Pushing straight to a bare URL hands that
   345		// URL to the hook as the remote arg, and git never records a
   346		// refs/remotes/<url>/* tracking ref for it — so a tracking-ref check would
   347		// defer the metadata forever. Publish for a non-configured (URL) target
   348		// rather than strand it; the first-branch scenario always uses a named
   349		// remote.
   350		if !isConfiguredRemote(ctx, ps.remote) {
   351			return false
   352		}

   354		// Known limitation, accepted for the no-network design: a tracking ref left
   355		// over from before a remote was deleted and recreated empty under the same
   356		// URL reads as "established", so v1 would publish to the now-empty remote.
   357		// Detecting that requires asking the remote — the network round trip we
   358		// deliberately avoid here. The scenario is rare and its default branch is
   359		// recoverable by resetting it on the forge.
   360		return !remoteHasTrackingRefs(ctx, ps.remote)
   361	}

   363	// isConfiguredRemote reports whether name is a configured git remote, as

   365	// URL directly. Local and best-effort (reads config, no network); any error is
   366	// treated as "not a configured remote".
   367	func isConfiguredRemote(ctx context.Context, name string) bool {

   369			return false
   370		}
   371		return cachedIsConfiguredRemote(ctx, name, func() (bool, error) {
   372			cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "remote", "get-url", name)
   373			if worktreeRoot, ok := settings.WorktreeRoot(ctx); ok {
   374				cmd.Dir = worktreeRoot
   375			}
   376			err := cmd.Run()
   377			if err == nil {
   378				return true, nil

   381			// all says nothing about the remote, and memoizing that false would
   382			// fail-close checkpoint_push_remote for the rest of the process.
   383			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
   384			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {

   417	// policy skips the ref push (leaving refs queued) rather than pushing.

   433		}

   435		// OPF backend divergence: both paths fail closed, but this one does it
   436		// without blocking the user. The v1 path aborts the user's git push; here a
   437		// checkpoint-ref failure must never do that (see this function's doc), so
   438		// failing closed means withholding the flush — nothing un-OPF'd ships, the
   439		// refs stay queued, and the user's push proceeds.

    48	// batchPushRefs pushes all of refs to target in a single git push,
    49	// fast-forward-only (NOT a force push). Batching keeps a backfill of many refs to
    50	// one network round-trip. Per-checkpoint refs normally advance by fast-forward
    51	// (each write parents on the prior tip), so the common case succeeds; a
    52	// non-fast-forward update — genuine divergence, e.g. the same checkpoint written
    53	// differently on another machine — is REJECTED rather than silently overwriting
    54	// the remote. We deliberately do not force: there is no server-side ref
    55	// protection, so a force push would make a buggy or racing client clobber good
    56	// remote history with no signal. On rejection the whole push errors; the caller
    57	// retries the rejected refs individually with fetch+replay recovery
    58	// (pushCheckpointRefWithRecovery).
    59	func batchPushRefs(ctx context.Context, target string, refs []plumbing.ReferenceName) error {
    60		if len(refs) == 0 {
    61			return nil
    62		}
    63		refSpecs := make([]string, 0, len(refs))
    64		for _, ref := range refs {
    65			refSpecs = append(refSpecs, ref.String()+":"+ref.String())
    66		}
    67		if _, err := remote.PushWithOptions(ctx, remote.PushOptions{Remote: target, RefSpecs: refSpecs}); err != nil {

    73	// pushCheckpointRefWithRecovery pushes a single checkpoint ref fast-forward-only;
    74	// on rejection — typically the ref diverged on the remote (the same checkpoint
    75	// re-written elsewhere) — it fetches the remote ref and replays the local-only
    76	// commits on top via fetchAndRebaseRefCommon, then retries. The retry is still
    77	// non-force: after the replay the local ref is a fast-forward over the remote, so
    78	// the remote commit is preserved as an ancestor rather than overwritten. The

    80	// (e.g. both sides rewrote the root metadata.json) surfaces as a rebase error and
    81	// the ref is left for a later pre-push. Returns nil only if the ref reached the

   652	// collectCommitsSince returns non-merge commits reachable from tip but not from
   653	// exclude, ordered oldest-first in topological order.
   654	func collectCommitsSince(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, repoPath string, tip, exclude plumbing.Hash) ([]*object.Commit, error) {
   655		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
   656		defer cancel()
   657	
   658		// cherryPickOnto computes each commit's delta against its first parent, so
   659		// replaying merge commits would incorrectly re-apply changes that arrived via
   660		// non-first-parent history. Limit the replay set to non-merge commits.
   661		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-list", "--reverse", "--topo-order", "--no-merges", exclude.String()+".."+tip.String())
   662		cmd.Dir = repoPath
   663		output, err := cmd.Output()
   664		if err != nil {
   665			return nil, fmt.Errorf("git rev-list failed: %w", err)
   666		}
   667	
   668		lines := strings.Fields(string(output))
   669		if len(lines) > MaxCommitTraversalDepth {
   670			return nil, fmt.Errorf("commit chain exceeded %d commits; aborting rebase", MaxCommitTraversalDepth)
   671		}
   672	
   673		commits := make([]*object.Commit, 0, len(lines))
   674		for _, line := range lines {
   675			hash := plumbing.NewHash(line)
   676			commit, commitErr := repo.CommitObject(hash)
   677			if commitErr != nil {
   678				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit %s: %w", hash, commitErr)
   679			}
   680			if len(commit.ParentHashes) > 1 {
   681				continue
   682			}
   683			commits = append(commits, commit)
   684		}
   685	
   686		return commits, nil
   687	}

   691	func startProgressDots(w io.Writer) func(suffix string) {
   692		done := make(chan struct{})
   693		stopped := make(chan struct{})
   694		go func() {
   695			defer close(stopped)

   697			defer ticker.Stop()
   698			for {

   701					return
   702				case <-ticker.C:
   703					fmt.Fprint(w, ".")
   704				}
   705			}

   709			<-stopped // Wait for goroutine to finish before writing suffix

   711		}

    48	// batchPushRefs pushes all of refs to target in a single git push,
    49	// fast-forward-only (NOT a force push). Batching keeps a backfill of many refs to
    50	// one network round-trip. Per-checkpoint refs normally advance by fast-forward
    51	// (each write parents on the prior tip), so the common case succeeds; a
    52	// non-fast-forward update — genuine divergence, e.g. the same checkpoint written
    53	// differently on another machine — is REJECTED rather than silently overwriting
    54	// the remote. We deliberately do not force: there is no server-side ref
    55	// protection, so a force push would make a buggy or racing client clobber good
    56	// remote history with no signal. On rejection the whole push errors; the caller
    57	// retries the rejected refs individually with fetch+replay recovery
    58	// (pushCheckpointRefWithRecovery).
    59	func batchPushRefs(ctx context.Context, target string, refs []plumbing.ReferenceName) error {
    60		if len(refs) == 0 {
    61			return nil
    62		}
    63		refSpecs := make([]string, 0, len(refs))
    64		for _, ref := range refs {
    65			refSpecs = append(refSpecs, ref.String()+":"+ref.String())
    66		}
    67		if _, err := remote.PushWithOptions(ctx, remote.PushOptions{Remote: target, RefSpecs: refSpecs}); err != nil {
    68			return fmt.Errorf("push %d checkpoint refs: %w", len(refs), err)
    69		}
    70		return nil
    71	}

    73	// pushCheckpointRefWithRecovery pushes a single checkpoint ref fast-forward-only;
    74	// on rejection — typically the ref diverged on the remote (the same checkpoint
    75	// re-written elsewhere) — it fetches the remote ref and replays the local-only
    76	// commits on top via fetchAndRebaseRefCommon, then retries. The retry is still
    77	// non-force: after the replay the local ref is a fast-forward over the remote, so
    78	// the remote commit is preserved as an ancestor rather than overwritten. The
    79	// cherry-pick is delta-based, so non-overlapping changes merge; a genuine overlap
    80	// (e.g. both sides rewrote the root metadata.json) surfaces as a rebase error and
    81	// the ref is left for a later pre-push. Returns nil only if the ref reached the
    82	// remote.
    83	func pushCheckpointRefWithRecovery(ctx context.Context, target string, ref plumbing.ReferenceName) error {
    84		// One shared budget across the initial push, fetch+replay, and retry, matching
    85		// doPushRef (fetchAndRebaseRefCommon relies on the caller's deadline).
    86		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, checkpointPushBudget)
    87		defer cancel()
    88	
    89		if err := batchPushRefs(ctx, target, []plumbing.ReferenceName{ref}); err == nil {
    90			return nil
    91		}
    92		if err := fetchAndRebaseRefCommon(ctx, target, ref); err != nil {
    93			return fmt.Errorf("sync diverged checkpoint ref %s: %w", ref, err)
    94		}
    95		return batchPushRefs(ctx, target, []plumbing.ReferenceName{ref})
    96	}

   108	func pushRefIfNeededWithMetadataThreshold(ctx context.Context, target string, ref plumbing.ReferenceName, metadataThreshold int64) (delivered bool, err error) {
   109		repo, err := OpenRepository(ctx)
   110		if err != nil {
   111			logging.Debug(ctx, "push skipped: open repository failed",
   112				slog.String("ref", ref.String()),
   113				slog.String("error", err.Error()))

   116		defer repo.Close()

   118		localRef, err := repo.Reference(ref, true)

   120			// Ref doesn't exist locally — nothing to push, and nothing delivered.
   121			// Reporting false rather than "vacuously delivered" keeps a caller that

   126		if ref.IsBranch() && !remote.IsURL(target) && !hasUnpushedBranchRef(repo, target, localRef.Hash(), ref.Short()) {

   128			// which is delivery as far as any caller can tell.
   129			return true, nil
   130		}
   131	
   132		return doPushRefWithMetadataThreshold(ctx, target, ref, metadataThreshold)
   133	}

   136	// Returns true if there's any difference that needs syncing (local ahead, remote ahead, or diverged).
   137	func hasUnpushedBranchRef(repo *git.Repository, remoteName string, localHash plumbing.Hash, branchName string) bool {

   139		remoteRefName := plumbing.NewRemoteReferenceName(remoteName, branchName)
   140		remoteRef, err := repo.Reference(remoteRefName, true)
   141		if err != nil {
   142			// Remote branch doesn't exist yet - we have content to push
   143			return true

   652	// collectCommitsSince returns non-merge commits reachable from tip but not from
   653	// exclude, ordered oldest-first in topological order.
   654	func collectCommitsSince(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, repoPath string, tip, exclude plumbing.Hash) ([]*object.Commit, error) {
   655		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
   656		defer cancel()
   657	
   658		// cherryPickOnto computes each commit's delta against its first parent, so
   659		// replaying merge commits would incorrectly re-apply changes that arrived via
   660		// non-first-parent history. Limit the replay set to non-merge commits.
   661		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-list", "--reverse", "--topo-order", "--no-merges", exclude.String()+".."+tip.String())
   662		cmd.Dir = repoPath
   663		output, err := cmd.Output()
   664		if err != nil {
   665			return nil, fmt.Errorf("git rev-list failed: %w", err)
   666		}
   667	
   668		lines := strings.Fields(string(output))
   669		if len(lines) > MaxCommitTraversalDepth {
   670			return nil, fmt.Errorf("commit chain exceeded %d commits; aborting rebase", MaxCommitTraversalDepth)
   671		}
   672	
   673		commits := make([]*object.Commit, 0, len(lines))
   674		for _, line := range lines {
   675			hash := plumbing.NewHash(line)
   676			commit, commitErr := repo.CommitObject(hash)
   677			if commitErr != nil {
   678				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit %s: %w", hash, commitErr)
   679			}
   680			if len(commit.ParentHashes) > 1 {
   681				continue
   682			}
   683			commits = append(commits, commit)
   684		}
   685	
   686		return commits, nil
   687	}

    48	// batchPushRefs pushes all of refs to target in a single git push,
    49	// fast-forward-only (NOT a force push). Batching keeps a backfill of many refs to
    50	// one network round-trip. Per-checkpoint refs normally advance by fast-forward
    51	// (each write parents on the prior tip), so the common case succeeds; a
    52	// non-fast-forward update — genuine divergence, e.g. the same checkpoint written
    53	// differently on another machine — is REJECTED rather than silently overwriting
    54	// the remote. We deliberately do not force: there is no server-side ref
    55	// protection, so a force push would make a buggy or racing client clobber good
    56	// remote history with no signal. On rejection the whole push errors; the caller
    57	// retries the rejected refs individually with fetch+replay recovery
    58	// (pushCheckpointRefWithRecovery).
    59	func batchPushRefs(ctx context.Context, target string, refs []plumbing.ReferenceName) error {
    60		if len(refs) == 0 {
    61			return nil
    62		}
    63		refSpecs := make([]string, 0, len(refs))
    64		for _, ref := range refs {
    65			refSpecs = append(refSpecs, ref.String()+":"+ref.String())
    66		}
    67		if _, err := remote.PushWithOptions(ctx, remote.PushOptions{Remote: target, RefSpecs: refSpecs}); err != nil {
    68			return fmt.Errorf("push %d checkpoint refs: %w", len(refs), err)
    69		}
    70		return nil
    71	}
    72	
    73	// pushCheckpointRefWithRecovery pushes a single checkpoint ref fast-forward-only;
    74	// on rejection — typically the ref diverged on the remote (the same checkpoint
    75	// re-written elsewhere) — it fetches the remote ref and replays the local-only
    76	// commits on top via fetchAndRebaseRefCommon, then retries. The retry is still
    77	// non-force: after the replay the local ref is a fast-forward over the remote, so
    78	// the remote commit is preserved as an ancestor rather than overwritten. The
    79	// cherry-pick is delta-based, so non-overlapping changes merge; a genuine overlap
    80	// (e.g. both sides rewrote the root metadata.json) surfaces as a rebase error and
    81	// the ref is left for a later pre-push. Returns nil only if the ref reached the
    82	// remote.
    83	func pushCheckpointRefWithRecovery(ctx context.Context, target string, ref plumbing.ReferenceName) error {
    84		// One shared budget across the initial push, fetch+replay, and retry, matching
    85		// doPushRef (fetchAndRebaseRefCommon relies on the caller's deadline).
    86		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, checkpointPushBudget)
    87		defer cancel()
    88	
    89		if err := batchPushRefs(ctx, target, []plumbing.ReferenceName{ref}); err == nil {
    90			return nil
    91		}
    92		if err := fetchAndRebaseRefCommon(ctx, target, ref); err != nil {
    93			return fmt.Errorf("sync diverged checkpoint ref %s: %w", ref, err)
    94		}
    95		return batchPushRefs(ctx, target, []plumbing.ReferenceName{ref})
    96	}

   100	// For branch refs, the "has unpushed" optimization consults the remote-tracking
   101	// ref. Non-branch refs and URL targets skip the optimization and let git
   102	// handle the no-op case.
