   108	func pushRefIfNeededWithMetadataThreshold(ctx context.Context, target string, ref plumbing.ReferenceName, metadataThreshold int64) (delivered bool, err error) {
   109		repo, err := OpenRepository(ctx)
   110		if err != nil {
   111			logging.Debug(ctx, "push skipped: open repository failed",
   112				slog.String("ref", ref.String()),
   113				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   114			return false, nil
   115		}
   116		defer repo.Close()
   117	
   118		localRef, err := repo.Reference(ref, true)
   119		if err != nil {
   120			// Ref doesn't exist locally — nothing to push, and nothing delivered.
   121			// Reporting false rather than "vacuously delivered" keeps a caller that
   122			// gates on delivery from acting on a ref that never existed.
   123			return false, nil
   124		}
   125	
   126		if ref.IsBranch() && !remote.IsURL(target) && !hasUnpushedBranchRef(repo, target, localRef.Hash(), ref.Short()) {
   127			// Local matches the target's tracking ref: the data is already there,
   128			// which is delivery as far as any caller can tell.
   129			return true, nil
   130		}
   131	
   132		return doPushRefWithMetadataThreshold(ctx, target, ref, metadataThreshold)
   133	}

   652	// collectCommitsSince returns non-merge commits reachable from tip but not from
   653	// exclude, ordered oldest-first in topological order.
   654	func collectCommitsSince(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, repoPath string, tip, exclude plumbing.Hash) ([]*object.Commit, error) {
   655		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
   656		defer cancel()
   657	
   658		// cherryPickOnto computes each commit's delta against its first parent, so
   659		// replaying merge commits would incorrectly re-apply changes that arrived via
   660		// non-first-parent history. Limit the replay set to non-merge commits.
   661		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-list", "--reverse", "--topo-order", "--no-merges", exclude.String()+".."+tip.String())
   662		cmd.Dir = repoPath
   663		output, err := cmd.Output()
   664		if err != nil {
   665			return nil, fmt.Errorf("git rev-list failed: %w", err)
   666		}
   667	
   668		lines := strings.Fields(string(output))
   669		if len(lines) > MaxCommitTraversalDepth {
   670			return nil, fmt.Errorf("commit chain exceeded %d commits; aborting rebase", MaxCommitTraversalDepth)
   671		}
   672	
   673		commits := make([]*object.Commit, 0, len(lines))
   674		for _, line := range lines {
   675			hash := plumbing.NewHash(line)
   676			commit, commitErr := repo.CommitObject(hash)
   677			if commitErr != nil {
   678				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit %s: %w", hash, commitErr)
   679			}
   680			if len(commit.ParentHashes) > 1 {
   681				continue
   682			}
   683			commits = append(commits, commit)
   684		}
   685	
   686		return commits, nil
   687	}

   365	// tryPushRefCommon attempts to push a ref. No timeout of its own —
   366	// runs under doPushRef's shared budget. Branch refs use a bare branch-name
   367	// refSpec so existing remote-tracking works; non-branch refs use an explicit
   368	// "refs/...:refs/..." refSpec with no tracking shadow. Neither forces: a
   369	// non-fast-forward is rejected so doPushRef's fetch+rebase recovery runs (and a
   370	// genuinely diverged ref is never silently overwritten — there is no
   371	// server-side ref protection). This keeps one consistent non-force policy for
   372	// every checkpoint ref, branch or per-checkpoint.
   373	func tryPushRefCommon(ctx context.Context, remoteName string, ref plumbing.ReferenceName) (pushResult, error) {
   374		refSpec := ref.Short()
   375		if !ref.IsBranch() {
   376			refSpec = ref.String() + ":" + ref.String()
   377		}
   378	
   379		// Span the actual `git push` subprocess: on a slow remote (e.g. a custom
   380		// git transport) this is typically where pre-push time is spent. Called once
   381		// per push attempt, so a retry after fetch+rebase shows up as a second
   382		// git_push step (git_push~1) in the trace. A rejected first push records an
   383		// error flag, which signals the recovery path was taken.
   384		_, pushSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "git_push")
   385		result, err := remote.Push(ctx, remoteName, refSpec)
   386		pushSpan.RecordError(err)
   387		pushSpan.End()
   388	
   389		outputStr := result.Output
   390		if err != nil {
   391			return pushResult{}, classifyPushFailure(ctx, outputStr, err)
   392		}
   393	
   394		return parsePushResult(outputStr), nil
   395	}

   580	// metadataRewriter rewrites a commit graph replacing oversized metadata.json
   581	// blobs. Every level is memoized: a blob is stripped once however many trees
   582	// reference it, a tree is rebuilt once however many commits share it, and a
   583	// commit is rewritten once however many children it has.
   584	type metadataRewriter struct {
   585		ctx       context.Context //nolint:containedctx // scoped to one rewrite; threaded into commit signing
   586		repo      *git.Repository
   587		threshold int64
   588	
   589		blobs   map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash
   590		trees   map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash
   591		commits map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash
   592	
   593		commitsRewritten int
   594		blobsShrunk      int
   595		stillOversized   []OversizedMetadataBlob
   596	}
   597	
   598	func newMetadataRewriter(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, threshold int64) *metadataRewriter {
   599		return &metadataRewriter{
   600			ctx:       ctx,
   601			repo:      repo,
   602			threshold: threshold,
   603			blobs:     make(map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash),
   604			trees:     make(map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash),
   605			commits:   make(map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash),
   606		}
   607	}
   608	
   609	// rewriteHistory returns the rewritten equivalent of tip. Parents are processed
   610	// before children with an explicit stack, so a branch with thousands of
   611	// checkpoints does not recurse thousands deep.
   612	func (r *metadataRewriter) rewriteHistory(tip plumbing.Hash) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   613		if tip.IsZero() {
   614			return tip, nil
   615		}
   616		type frame struct {
   617			hash     plumbing.Hash
   618			expanded bool
   619		}
   620		stack := []frame{{hash: tip}}
   621		for len(stack) > 0 {
   622			if err := r.ctx.Err(); err != nil {
   623				return plumbing.ZeroHash, err //nolint:wrapcheck // context cancellation propagates as-is
   624			}
   625			top := len(stack) - 1
   626			f := stack[top]
   627			if _, done := r.commits[f.hash]; done {
   628				stack = stack[:top]
   629				continue
   630			}
   631			c, err := r.repo.CommitObject(f.hash)
   632			if err != nil {
   633				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("load commit %s: %w", f.hash, err)
   634			}
   635			if !f.expanded {
   636				stack[top].expanded = true
   637				for _, p := range c.ParentHashes {
   638					if _, done := r.commits[p]; !done {
   639						stack = append(stack, frame{hash: p})
   640					}
   641				}
   642				continue
   643			}
   644			newHash, err := r.rewriteCommit(c)
   645			if err != nil {
   646				return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   647			}
   648			r.commits[f.hash] = newHash
   649			stack = stack[:top]
   650		}
   651		return r.commits[tip], nil
   652	}
   653	
   654	func (r *metadataRewriter) rewriteCommit(c *object.Commit) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   655		newTree, err := r.rewriteTree(c.TreeHash, "")
   656		if err != nil {
   657			return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   658		}
   659		parents := make([]plumbing.Hash, 0, len(c.ParentHashes))

   662			np, ok := r.commits[p]
   663			if !ok {
   664				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("parent %s of %s was not rewritten first", p, c.Hash)
   665			}
   666			if !np.Equal(p) {
   667				changed = true
   668			}
   669			parents = append(parents, np)
   670		}
   671		if !changed {
   672			return c.Hash, nil
   673		}

   676			Committer:    c.Committer,
   677			Message:      c.Message,
   678			TreeHash:     newTree,
   679			ParentHashes: parents,
   680			Encoding:     c.Encoding,
   681			ExtraHeaders: c.ExtraHeaders,
   682		}

   684		// original tree, so it cannot be carried over. Signing makes the rewritten
   685		// hash non-deterministic across runs, which is why reconciliation below
   686		// compares trees (contentReachable) rather than hashes.
   687		checkpoint.SignCommitBestEffort(r.ctx, rewritten)
   688		obj := r.repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
   689		if err := rewritten.Encode(obj); err != nil {
   690			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("encode rewritten commit %s: %w", c.Hash, err)
   691		}
   692		hash, err := r.repo.Storer.SetEnco…852 tokens truncated…merge commits would incorrectly re-apply changes that arrived via
   660		// non-first-parent history. Limit the replay set to non-merge commits.
   661		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-list", "--reverse", "--topo-order", "--no-merges", exclude.String()+".."+tip.String())
   662		cmd.Dir = repoPath
   663		output, err := cmd.Output()
   664		if err != nil {
   665			return nil, fmt.Errorf("git rev-list failed: %w", err)
   666		}
   667	
   668		lines := strings.Fields(string(output))
   669		if len(lines) > MaxCommitTraversalDepth {
   670			return nil, fmt.Errorf("commit chain exceeded %d commits; aborting rebase", MaxCommitTraversalDepth)
   671		}
   672	
   673		commits := make([]*object.Commit, 0, len(lines))
   674		for _, line := range lines {
   675			hash := plumbing.NewHash(line)
   676			commit, commitErr := repo.CommitObject(hash)
   677			if commitErr != nil {
   678				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit %s: %w", hash, commitErr)
   679			}
   680			if len(commit.ParentHashes) > 1 {
   681				continue
   682			}
   683			commits = append(commits, commit)
   684		}
   685	
   686		return commits, nil
   687	}

   689	// startProgressDots prints dots to w every second until the returned stop function
   690	// is called. The stop function prints the given suffix and a newline.
   691	func startProgressDots(w io.Writer) func(suffix string) {
   692		done := make(chan struct{})
   693		stopped := make(chan struct{})
   694		go func() {
   695			defer close(stopped)
   696			ticker := time.NewTicker(time.Second)
   697			defer ticker.Stop()
   698			for {
   699				select {
   700				case <-done:
   701					return
   702				case <-ticker.C:
   703					fmt.Fprint(w, ".")
   704				}
   705			}
   706		}()
   707		return func(suffix string) {
   708			close(done)
   709			<-stopped // Wait for goroutine to finish before writing suffix
   710			fmt.Fprintln(w, suffix)
   711		}
   712	}

    12	// PersistentRefs is the committed-metadata ref topology.
    13	type PersistentRefs struct {
    14		Primary plumbing.ReferenceName
    15		Read    plumbing.ReferenceName
    16		Push    []plumbing.ReferenceName
    17	
    18		// localReadOnly pins reads to the local Read ref with no remote-tracking
    19		// tiers at all — set via PrimaryAsLocalRead. Guards (attach's
    20		// local-presence gates) that must answer "would the next LOCAL write see
    21		// this checkpoint?" need it: the ordinary read chain selects per
    22		// checkpoint across local and remote-tracking trees, so a checkpoint
    23		// present only on a remote would otherwise read as present and a write
    24		// based on the stale local branch would clobber the remote on push.
    25		localReadOnly bool
    26	}
    27	
    28	// DefaultV1Refs returns the v1-only topology.
    29	func DefaultV1Refs() PersistentRefs {
    30		v1Branch := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName)
    31		return PersistentRefs{
    32			Primary: v1Branch,
    33			Read:    v1Branch,
    34			Push:    []plumbing.ReferenceName{v1Branch},
    35		}
    36	}
    37	
    38	// PrimaryFetchableFromRemote reports whether Primary has a remote-tracking
    39	// shadow on whichever remote carries checkpoint data (the caller supplies the
    40	// remote-tracking ref).
    41	func (r PersistentRefs) PrimaryFetchableFromRemote() bool {
    42		return r.Primary.IsBranch() && slices.Contains(r.Push, r.Primary)
    43	}
    44	
    45	// ReadBootstrappableFromRemote reports whether reads can be bootstrapped from
    46	// whichever remote carries checkpoint data (the caller supplies the
    47	// remote-tracking ref): true when reads target Primary and Primary is
    48	// fetchable from a remote, and the topology was not pinned local-only.
    49	func (r PersistentRefs) ReadBootstrappableFromRemote() bool {
    50		return !r.localReadOnly && r.Read == r.Primary && r.PrimaryFetchableFromRemote()
    51	}
    52	
    53	// PrimaryAsRead returns a copy of r with Read pinned to Primary.
    54	func (r PersistentRefs) PrimaryAsRead() PersistentRefs {
    55		r.Read = r.Primary
    56		return r
    57	}
    58	
    59	// PrimaryAsLocalRead returns a copy of r with Read pinned to Primary and
    60	// every remote read tier disabled — see the localReadOnly field for when a
    61	// caller needs this instead of PrimaryAsRead.
    62	func (r PersistentRefs) PrimaryAsLocalRead() PersistentRefs {
    63		r.Read = r.Primary
    64		r.localReadOnly = true
    65		return r
    66	}
    67	
    68	// ResolveRefs returns the committed metadata topology.
    69	func ResolveRefs(_ context.Context) PersistentRefs {
    70		return DefaultV1Refs()
    71	}

   171	// the commit graph — but every caller here passes true, and the reason is worth
   172	// stating because the cheaper option looks safe and is not.
   173	//
   174	// Filtering would be correct only where nothing downstream reads blob content
   175	// from the local branch. No caller meets that bar: each one lands v1 as the
   176	// repo's checkpoint store, and GitStore.List reads each checkpoint's
   177	// metadata.json through a plain tree with no blob fetcher attached. Worse, the
   178	// read path's recovery tier is keyed on the *ref* being missing, so once a
   179	// filtered fetch lands the ref it never fires again — leaving `checkpoint list`
   180	// permanently showing bare IDs with no prompt, date, or counts, recoverable only
   181	// by explaining each checkpoint by ID.
   182	//
   183	// The parameter is kept rather than inlined so the contract stays explicit at

   185	// timeout bounds the fetch: pass checkpointRemoteFetchTimeout on the push hot

   197			Dir:      dir,

   200			return nil
   201		}
   202	
   203		redactedURL := remote.RedactURL(remoteURL)
   204		msg := strings.TrimSpace(strings.ReplaceAll(string(output), remoteURL, redactedURL))
   205		if msg != "" {
   206			return fmt.Errorf("fetch %s from %s failed: %s: %w", label, redactedURL, msg, fetchErr)

   213	// It runs on the push hot path, so it uses the short fetch budget.

   215	// A fetch failure is not fatal — the push will create the branch on the remote
   216	// when it succeeds — but it is returned rather than swallowed so the caller can
   217	// log it. Returning nil unconditionally meant a checkpoint remote that was

   225	// treating every fetch error as absence.

1	package strategy
     2	
     3	import (
     4		"context"
     5		"fmt"
     6		"log/slog"
     7	
     8		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/remote"
     9		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
    10	)
    11	
    12	// refsPushDestination is the single place checkpoint refs are pushed to.
    13	type refsPushDestination struct {
    14		// target is passed to git push and to the recovery fetch: a remote name, or a URL.
    15		target string
    16		// checkpointRemote records that target came from a configured
    17		// checkpoint_remote. It cannot be recovered from target's shape — a
    18		// resolved push URL is URL-shaped too — and it decides both how the
    19		// destination is named and whether the "a checkpoint remote is configured"
    20		// hint applies.
    21		checkpointRemote bool
    22		// ignoredPushURLs counts the push URLs of a multi-URL remote that will NOT
    23		// receive checkpoint refs. Zero in every single-destination topology.
    24		ignoredPushURLs int
    25	}
    26	
    27	// resolveRefsPushDestination picks the single destination for checkpoint-ref
    28	// pushes.
    29	//
    30	// Checkpoint refs need ONE deterministic destination, because the push-discovery
    31	// queue records only a ref (`{"ref": …}`) with no per-destination state: a ref is
    32	// removed from the queue once "the push" succeeds, so "the push" has to mean one
